member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.ICanvasHandler
member.summary: Provider-side canvas lifecycle handler.
member.remarks:
A session installs a single via SessionConfigBase.CanvasHandler. The handler receives every inbound canvas.open / canvas.close / canvas.action.invoke JSON-RPC request the runtime issues for this session and decides — typically by inspecting — which application-side canvas should handle the call.
The SDK does not maintain a per-canvas registry; multiplexing across declared canvases is the implementor's responsibility.
Implementations targeting netstandard2.0 cannot rely on default interface methods; derive from to inherit sensible defaults for and .

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.CopilotClient.StartAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Starts the Copilot client and connects to the server.
member.param: A that can be used to cancel the operation.
member.returns: A representing the asynchronous operation.
member.remarks: If the server is not already running and the client is configured to spawn one (default), it will be started. If connecting to an external runtime (via RuntimeConnection.ForUri), only establishes the connection. If a previous start failed or was canceled, calling this method again starts the client anew.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.CopilotClient.StopAsync
member.summary: Disconnects from the Copilot server and closes all active sessions.
member.returns: A representing the asynchronous operation.

remarks.para:
This method performs graceful cleanup:
Closes all active sessions (releases in-memory resources); detach requests share one shutdown timeout, so an unresponsive runtime cannot hold the remaining steps back
Requests runtime shutdown for SDK-owned CLI processes
Closes the JSON-RPC connection
Terminates the CLI server process (if spawned by this client)
Note: session data on disk is preserved, so sessions can be resumed later. To permanently remove session data before stopping, call for each session first.

member.exception: Thrown when multiple errors occur during cleanup.

example.code: await client.StopAsync();

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.CopilotClient.ForceStopAsync
member.summary: Forces an immediate stop of the client without graceful cleanup.
member.returns: A representing the asynchronous operation.
member.remarks:
Use this when fails or takes too long. This method:
Clears all sessions immediately without destroying them
Stops session event delivery without waiting for running handlers
Force closes the connection
Kills the CLI process (if spawned by this client)

member.summary: Creates a , wires up handlers from the session config, registers it with the client, and starts its event processing loop. Used by both (invoked from the JSON-RPC read loop the instant the response arrives, so that session events delivered between the response and the awaiter resuming are not dropped) and (invoked before the RPC is issued, since the session id is known up front).

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.FfiRuntimeHost
member.summary: Hosts the Copilot runtime in-process by loading the Rust cdylib (runtime.node) and speaking JSON-RPC over its C ABI (FFI) instead of spawning a CLI child process and communicating over stdio/TCP.
member.remarks:
The Rust host_start export constructs the server synchronously in this process. JSON-RPC frames are pumped across the ABI: writes go to connection_write; inbound frames arrive on a native callback that feeds .
The native interop layer has two implementations selected by target framework. On modern .NET it uses source-generated LibraryImport P/Invoke with an UnmanagedCallersOnly function-pointer callback, which is trim- and NativeAOT-compatible. On netstandard2.0 (which has neither LibraryImport nor NativeLibrary) it falls back to classic delegate-based P/Invoke over a hand-rolled dlopen/LoadLibrary loader. Because the library lives at a runtime-resolved absolute path, the modern path maps the logical via a resolver and the legacy path loads the absolute path directly.

member.summary: The stream JSON-RPC reads server→client frames from.

member.summary: The stream JSON-RPC writes client→server frames to.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ConnectRequest.EnableGitHubTelemetryForwarding
member.summary: Opt this connection in to GitHub telemetry forwarding for its lifetime. When set, the runtime forwards this host's telemetry across all its sessions, its sessionless events, and explicitly process-wide events over the `gitHubTelemetry.event` notification. Connections intentionally sharing one server receive that server's events; independently embedded runtime hosts do not receive each other's host-owned events. Regular events are also written to the runtime's normal GitHub/CTS path (dual-write); host-only compatibility events are forward-only and intentionally skip that path. Intended for first-party hosts that re-emit the events into their own telemetry stores. Both unrestricted and restricted events are forwarded, each tagged with a `restricted` discriminator; a backstop drops restricted events when restricted telemetry is disabled — using the process-global gate for ordinary events and an explicit session-scoped decision for host-only events.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ConnectRequest.Entra

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ConnectRequest.EntraTokenProvider
member.summary: Opt this connection in to host-owned Entra identity and token acquisition through entraToken.getToken. Requires entra.clientId and an explicit true acknowledgement in the response. SDKs set this internally when a callback is configured.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxHostCapability
member.summary: Whether this host can run one sandbox policy feature. A session whose effective policy uses an unsupported feature fails each sandboxed command with `reason`, except `filesystem_enumeration`, whose absence degrades sandboxed PowerShell instead of failing it.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxHostCapability.Name
member.summary: The policy feature, as an extensible string: ignore names you do not recognize. Known values: `network` (sandboxed commands can reach the network; on Linux this needs the tooling for Bubblewrap's private network namespace, such as slirp4netns), `network_filtering` (host rules and the sandbox proxy; on Linux this needs the same tooling as `network`; on Windows it needs Process Security Environment 1.1 host-loopback support or MXC's PSEC 1.0-only proxy-loopback compatibility capability, and a policy that uses it must also set `network.allowLocalNetwork`; compatibility applies only to an explicit identity-less runtime proxy, not general host-loopback access, and other policy restrictions still apply), `denied_paths` (native enforcement of `filesystem.deniedPaths`), `shell` (shell commands inside the sandbox), and `filesystem_enumeration` (enumerate-only filesystem grants: PowerShell's drive roots and `filesystem.enumeratePaths`; on Windows this needs Process Security Environment 1.1 filesystem enumeration support, and without it sandboxed PowerShell still runs but cannot resolve its current location, and `filesystem.enumeratePaths` entries are ignored; other platforms always report it).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxHostCapability.Reason
member.summary: Human-readable reason and remedy when the feature is unsupported, such as a package to install or an OS update. Present only when `supported` is false.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxHostCapability.Supported
member.summary: Whether this host can run the feature.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxHostSupport
member.summary: Whether the host running this runtime can run the command sandbox. The runtime checks `supported` once per process. A capability answer can change while the process runs, for example after the user installs a missing package.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxHostSupport.Capabilities
member.summary: Sandbox policy features whose availability varies between hosts that can run the backend. Empty when `supported` is false, because no feature can run without a backend. Later runtimes can add entries; ignore an entry whose `name` you do not recognize.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxHostSupport.Reason
member.summary: Human-readable reason the sandbox cannot run on this host. Present only when `supported` is false.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxHostSupport.Supported
member.summary: Whether a process-containment backend is usable on this host: Seatbelt on macOS, Bubblewrap on Linux, or ProcessContainer on Windows.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigAuth
member.summary: Credential-injection capability flags applied while the sandbox is enabled. For the same capability independent of sandboxing, and matched to the credential's GitHub host, see `shell.credentials`; the two are additive.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigAuth.Gh
member.summary: Whether to authenticate sandboxed gh through the local masking proxy. The child receives a fake GH_TOKEN; its real value is substituted only at github.com, api.github.com and uploads.github.com (github.com because gh repo clone authenticates git through gh auth git-credential). The repository's GitHub account takes precedence over the Copilot login. Default: false (opt-in).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigAuth.Git
member.summary: Whether to authenticate sandboxed HTTPS git through the local masking proxy. The child receives a fake `http.<url>.extraheader`; the real Authorization header is substituted only at its original HTTPS host, port, and repository path scope. github.com uses the Copilot token; other forges use credentials resolved from the user's own helper on the host. Default: false (opt-in).

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxMaskedEnvVar
member.summary: Destinations authorized to receive one masked environment credential.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxMaskedEnvVar.InjectHosts
member.summary: Nonempty list of HTTPS injection hostnames or *.example.com patterns. Bare * is not accepted. These grants never override the sandbox network policy. Values in plaintext HTTP requests, URLs, bodies, encoded credentials, and signed requests are not substituted.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxCredentialsConfig
member.summary: Whole-value environment credential masking for sandboxed children.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxCredentialsConfig.EnvVars
member.summary: Environment variable names and their HTTPS injection destinations. Absent variables stay absent. No real values or sentinels are stored in this map.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyExperimental.Seatbelt
member.summary: macOS seatbelt experimental options.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyFilesystem
member.summary: Filesystem rules to merge into the base policy.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyFilesystem.DeniedPaths
member.summary: Paths explicitly denied.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyFilesystem.EnumeratePaths
member.summary: Paths granted enumerate-only access: sandboxed commands can list these directories without reading the files in them. Honored only on Windows hosts with the `filesystem_enumeration` capability; ignored elsewhere. An entry at or under a read-only, read-write, or denied path is ignored, so it never narrows a grant or reopens a denial.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyFilesystem.ReadonlyPaths
member.summary: Paths granted read-only access.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyNetworkProxy
member.summary: HTTP proxy configuration for sandboxed traffic.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyNetworkProxy.Password
member.summary: Optional password for proxy authentication, combined with the URL at spawn time. The persisted value may be a literal password, a `${secret:…}` reference resolved from the OS keychain, or a `${VAR}`/`$VAR` environment reference; it is resolved just before the sandboxed process routes through the proxy. The /sandbox dialog stores a real password in the OS keychain and persists only a `${secret:…}` placeholder (never plaintext in settings.json); the field is masked in the dialog and redacted by /settings show.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyNetworkProxy.Url
member.summary: Proxy URL (e.g. http://proxy.example.com:8080). The port is optional and defaults to the scheme's standard port when omitted; an explicit port must be between 1 and 65535. Credentials must not be embedded here — a `user:pass@` authority is rejected; put them in the separate `username`/`password` fields. A credential-free http:// loopback proxy URL is routed through the localhost proxy automatically; loopback covers localhost and any *.localhost subdomain, the whole 127.0.0.0/8 range, ::1, and IPv4-mapped loopback (::ffff:127.0.0.1). An https:// URL, or one with a username/password set, is used as-is.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyNetworkProxy.Username
member.summary: Optional username for proxy authentication. Combined with the URL (and `password`) into `user:pass@host` when the sandboxed process routes through the proxy.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyNetwork
member.summary: Network rules to merge into the base policy.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyNetwork.AllowedHosts
member.summary: Destinations allowed through the built-in sandbox proxy. Supports hostnames, IP addresses, IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs (10.0.0.0/8, fd00::/8), and *.example.com for strict subdomains. CIDR host bits must be zero; invalid entries suggest the network address. Within each nonempty list, matching names or addresses are alternative grants; every user and managed list must permit every resolved address. Empty lists add no restriction. Host rules never override outbound or local-network toggles. An upstream proxy owns DNS: CIDR-only grants cannot authorize unresolved names, and address denials cannot constrain its resolver.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyNetwork.AllowLocalNetwork
member.summary: Whether host-local destinations, including loopback and unspecified addresses, are allowed. Private networks follow outbound and host rules. Host rules still apply.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyNetwork.AllowOutbound
member.summary: Whether outbound network destinations, including private networks, are allowed. Host-loopback access is controlled separately by allowLocalNetwork. Host rules still apply.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyNetwork.BlockedHosts
member.summary: Destinations denied by the built-in sandbox proxy. Deny overrides allowedHosts, including CIDR denials against allowed names and their resolved addresses. Supports exact IPs and IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs with zero host bits. A denied domain also denies its subdomains; *.example.com matches strict subdomains, and * denies every host. With upstream-owned DNS, address denials cannot constrain remotely resolved names.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicyNetwork.Proxy
member.summary: HTTP(S) proxy for sandboxed traffic. This is the built-in local proxy's upstream: every sandboxed command reaches it through a loopback listener, so credentials stay in the runtime and never reach the child. On Windows the sandbox also needs local network access, because it reaches that listener over host loopback. Configure credentials in the separate username/password fields. The transient local listener URL is never persisted.

member.summary: macOS seatbelt-specific options.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicySeatbelt.KeychainAccess
member.summary: Whether the macOS seatbelt profile may access the keychain.

member.summary: Filesystem rules to merge into the base policy.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfigUserPolicy.Network
member.summary: Network rules to merge into the base policy.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfig
member.summary: Resolved sandbox configuration.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfig.AddCurrentWorkingDirectory
member.summary: Whether to auto-add the current working directory to readwritePaths. Default: true.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfig.AllowBypass
member.summary: Whether the agent may request that an individual command run outside the sandbox, which the host then approves or denies through the usual permission flow. A host capability flag rather than part of the policy: it is stripped from the effective spawn policy and only has an effect while `enabled` is true. Fail-closed, unlike the opt-out flags on this object: omitting it offers no bypass. Default: false (opt-in).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfig.AllowDevToolAccess
member.summary: Whether to auto-grant read access to tool directories discovered on PATH and in toolchain environment variables (GOROOT, JAVA_HOME, VIRTUAL_ENV, and similar), and to common developer-tool caches, config, and toolchains. Writable grants cover scratch caches, the Unix GitHub CLI cache, and Cargo's registry, git store, and lock/tracker files. A relocated CARGO_HOME gets the same narrow split: registry and git are read-write; bin is read-only; the home root, config.toml, and credentials.toml stay ungranted. Set to false to disable every grant listed above; user-installed toolchains and caches then need explicit userPolicy.filesystem readonlyPaths and readwritePaths entries. The working directory (see addCurrentWorkingDirectory), temporary storage, session log paths, and system locations follow their own rules and stay granted. Default: true (enabled by default; set to false to opt out).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfig.Auth
member.summary: Credential-injection capability flags.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfig.Credentials
member.summary: Opt-in whole-value environment masking for sandboxed shell, MCP, and LSP children. Configured names get random sentinels; the local proxy substitutes them only in HTTPS request headers at their injection hosts. Approved bypasses skip masking and the sandbox proxy, so bypassed shells may receive the real environment values. Disabled or explicitly opted-out routes are not protected. No credential values are stored in this configuration.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfig.Enabled
member.summary: Whether sandboxing is enabled for the session.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfig.ManagedExtensionsRoutingLocked
member.summary: The `sandboxExtensions` counterpart of `managedMcpRoutingLocked`.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfig.ManagedLspRoutingLocked
member.summary: The `sandboxLspServers` counterpart of `managedMcpRoutingLocked`.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfig.ManagedMcpRoutingLocked
member.summary: Set by the runtime when a managed policy forced `sandboxMcpServers` on and took the local opt-out away. Provenance rather than policy: it lets a sandbox startup failure point at the administrator instead of a setting the next managed merge would override, and it is ignored when comparing two configs for change. Only the managed merge may set it; a caller-supplied value is stripped.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfig.SandboxExtensions
member.summary: Whether extension processes the session launches are confined by the sandbox. Only an explicit `false` opts out. Ignored while `enabled` is false. Default: true (enabled by default; set to false to opt out).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfig.SandboxLspServers
member.summary: Whether language servers the session launches are confined by the sandbox. Only an explicit `false` opts out. Ignored while `enabled` is false. Default: true (enabled by default; set to false to opt out).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxConfig.SandboxMcpServers
member.summary: Whether MCP servers the session launches are confined by the sandbox. Only an explicit `false` opts out; doing so also lets remote-MCP egress leave the sandbox, so the flag and `enabled` are always read together. Ignored while `enabled` is false. Default: true (enabled by default; set to false to opt out).

member.summary: User-managed sandbox policy fragment merged into the auto-discovered base policy.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsSetHookDisabledRequest
member.summary: One hook to disable or re-enable.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadForConfigDirRequest
member.summary: Selects the configuration directory whose user settings to read.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadForConfigDirRequest.ConfigDir
member.summary: Copilot configuration directory to read the settings document from, taking precedence over the server's own `COPILOT_HOME` and default home. Omit it, or pass an empty string, to read the directory the server resolved for itself.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadRepoResult
member.summary: A repository's settings as stored, together with any diagnostic raised while reading them.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadRepoResult.Settings
member.summary: The repository's settings document, keyed by setting name, with each value carried verbatim. Null when the repository declares no settings.

member.summary: Why part of the document was ignored, as a single human-readable string joining every diagnostic with `; `. Null when the document loaded cleanly. The settings that did load are still reported, so a consumer should surface this and continue rather than treat it as a failure.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadRepoRequest
member.summary: Selects the repository whose checked-in settings to read.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadRepoRequest.RepoRoot
member.summary: Absolute path of the repository root whose settings to read. When this is the user's home directory, the Claude-compatible configuration is skipped, so a home-directory session does not inherit a personal config as if it were repository policy.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadAndMergeRepoResult
member.summary: The settings a consumer should act on inside a repository, together with any diagnostic raised while reading the repository layer.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadAndMergeRepoResult.Settings
member.summary: The merged settings document, keyed by setting name. Equals the supplied user layer when the repository declares no settings.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadAndMergeRepoResult.Warning
member.summary: Why part of the repository document was ignored, as a single human-readable string joining every diagnostic with `; `. Null when it loaded cleanly. The settings that did load are still merged, so a consumer should surface this and continue rather than treat it as a failure.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadAndMergeRepoRequest
member.summary: A repository to read settings from, and the user layer they are merged over.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadAndMergeRepoRequest.RepoRoot
member.summary: Absolute path of the repository root whose settings to read. When this is the user's home directory, the Claude-compatible configuration is skipped, so a home-directory session does not inherit a personal config as if it were repository policy.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadAndMergeRepoRequest.UserSettings
member.summary: The user's own settings, keyed by setting name. The repository layer is merged over this; a repository may only add to the collection settings it is allowed to influence, so a user setting it does not name survives unchanged.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsPathResult
member.summary: The on-disk location of the user's settings document.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsPathResult.Path
member.summary: Absolute path to the settings file this runtime reads and writes. Normally `settings.json` under the Copilot configuration directory; an extensionless legacy `settings` file is reported instead when it exists and `settings.json` does not.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadWithWarningResult
member.summary: The user's stored settings, together with any diagnostic raised while reading them.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadWithWarningResult.Settings
member.summary: The stored user settings document, keyed by setting name, with each value carried verbatim. Empty when the file could not be read at all.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsLoadWithWarningResult.Warning
member.summary: Why part of the document was ignored, phrased for display to the user. Null when the document loaded cleanly. The settings that did load are still reported, so a consumer may surface this and continue rather than treat it as a failure.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMergeManagedAndUserResult
member.summary: The user layer folded over the managed layer.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMergeManagedAndUserResult.SettingsJson
member.summary: The merged settings. An empty object when neither layer was supplied, so an unmanaged host with no user settings governs nothing.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMergeManagedAndUserParams
member.summary: The managed (enterprise policy) layer and the user layer to fold together. The field names carry the layer identity: nothing about a settings object identifies which layer produced it, so a generic base/override pair would let a caller transpose them and silently resolve the governance keys in the user's favour.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMergeManagedAndUserParams.Managed
member.summary: The managed layer. Its governance keys win, and the per-entry `enabledPlugins` and `extraKnownMarketplaces` control maps are stamped back from it after the union. Omitted when the host is unmanaged.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMergeManagedAndUserParams.User
member.summary: The user's own settings layer. Wins on every key the managed layer does not govern. Omitted when the user has no settings yet.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMergeRepoValueResult
member.summary: The repository layer folded into the user layer.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMergeRepoValueResult.SettingsJson
member.summary: The merged settings, with the per-entry managed control maps re-stamped from the runtime's ambient managed policy.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMergeRepoValueParams
member.summary: The user layer and the repository layer to fold together.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMergeRepoValueParams.RepoSettings
member.summary: The repository's checked-in settings layer.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMergeRepoValueParams.UserSettings
member.summary: The user's settings, already resolved against any managed layer.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMigrateStaffUpdateChannelOnceResult

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMigrateStaffUpdateChannelOnceResult.Status

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsHostContext
member.summary: The filesystem and environment facts a user-settings file is resolved from. Passed explicitly rather than read from the runtime's own process, so a host whose configuration directory differs from its process environment resolves the file it means.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsHostContext.ConfigDir
member.summary: The Copilot configuration directory, when the host set one. Takes precedence over `COPILOT_HOME` and the home directory.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsHostContext.Environment
member.summary: The host's environment variables. `COPILOT_HOME` is read from here, as are the variables a settings hook may expand.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsHostContext.HomeDirectory
member.summary: The user's home directory, used when neither a configuration directory nor `COPILOT_HOME` is set.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsResetStaffModelSelectionOnceResult
member.summary: The outcome of the one-time staff model-selection reset.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsResetStaffModelSelectionOnceResult.Cutoff
member.summary: The cutoff this reset is gated on, as an ISO-8601 timestamp. A recorded timestamp at or after it means the reset is already done.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsResetStaffModelSelectionOnceResult.DidReset
member.summary: Whether the persisted model selection was cleared. Only `true` means the settings document changed and the host should adopt the returned settings.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsResetStaffModelSelectionOnceResult.ResetAt
member.summary: The timestamp the host should now record, as an ISO-8601 timestamp. Carries the caller's own value back unchanged when nothing was reset.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsResetStaffModelSelectionOnceResult.Settings
member.summary: The settings document as it stands after the reset, keyed by setting name. Present only when `didReset` is true.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsResetStaffModelSelectionOnceRequest
member.summary: Selects the configuration directory to run the one-time staff model-selection reset against, and supplies the caller's record of whether it has already run.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsResetStaffModelSelectionOnceRequest.Context
member.summary: The configuration directory, home directory and environment to resolve the settings and global-state documents from. A host that scopes a session to its own Copilot home must pass that directory here, or the reset is evaluated against the server's own home instead.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsResetStaffModelSelectionOnceRequest.Staff
member.summary: Whether the signed-in account is a staff account. The reset applies only to staff, so anything other than `true` returns `didReset: false` without touching the settings document.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsResetStaffModelSelectionOnceRequest.StaffModelResetAt
member.summary: When the caller last recorded this reset, as an ISO-8601 timestamp. A timestamp at or after the cutoff means the reset already ran and is returned unchanged.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsUnknownKeysWarningResult
member.summary: The unrecognized top-level keys found in the user settings document, already phrased for display.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsUnknownKeysWarningResult.Warning
member.summary: The warning to show the user, naming the unrecognized keys and the file they were found in. Absent when every top-level key is recognized, and also when the document is missing or could not be read, because an unknown-key list taken from a document the runtime could not load would name keys that may not be there.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsUnknownKeysWarningRequest
member.summary: Selects the configuration directory whose user settings document should be inspected for unrecognized top-level keys.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsUnknownKeysWarningRequest.Context
member.summary: The configuration directory, home directory and environment to resolve the settings document from. A host that scopes a session to its own Copilot home must pass that directory here, or the server's own home is inspected instead.

member.summary: The overrides and host context to resolve effective runtime settings from.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsBuildRuntimeRequest.Environment
member.summary: The environment to read settings-bearing variables from. Passed explicitly rather than read from the server process so a host can resolve settings for an environment it is about to create rather than the one it runs in.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsBuildRuntimeRequest.Overrides
member.summary: Settings that take precedence over every document and environment layer, such as the values a host derived from its own command line. Keyed by setting name, with each value carried verbatim, so a host may pass keys this runtime does not recognize. Absent when the host contributes no overrides of its own.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsBuildRuntimeRequest.Platform
member.summary: The platform to apply platform-specific defaults for, in the same spelling the host's own runtime reports.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsBuildRuntimeRequest.WorkingDirectory
member.summary: The directory the settings are being resolved for. This selects the repository-scoped document, so a host resolving settings for a directory other than its own process working directory must pass that directory here.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMigrateStaffLogLevelOnceResult
member.summary: The outcome of the one-time staff log-level migration.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMigrateStaffLogLevelOnceResult.CompletedAt
member.summary: When the migration was recorded as done, as an ISO-8601 timestamp. Absent only for `ineligible`, which records nothing.

member.summary: The configuration directory, home directory and environment to resolve the settings and global-state documents from. A host that scopes a session to its own Copilot home must pass that directory here, or the migration is evaluated against the server's own home instead.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMigrateObsoleteOnDiskResult
member.summary: The outcome of the one-time obsolete-settings cleanup.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMigrateObsoleteOnDiskResult.Status
member.summary: What the cleanup did. Only `changed` rewrote the document. The cleaned settings are not returned here: the document is written before this replies, so `user.settings.load` reads it authoritatively.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMigrateObsoleteOnDiskRequest
member.summary: Selects the configuration directory whose settings document to clean.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UserSettingsMigrateObsoleteOnDiskRequest.ConfigDir
member.summary: The configuration directory holding the settings document to clean. A host that scopes a session to its own Copilot home passes that directory here; omit it to clean the document under the home the server resolved for itself. The home directory and environment are deliberately not caller-supplied: they decide only the settings path root and the two hook-parsing flags, and those describe the process doing the reading rather than the caller.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.PolicyHelperLoadFailed
member.summary: The policy helper was configured but could not be run or its output could not be read.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.PolicyHelperResponse
member.summary: The layer produced by the platform policy helper, when one ran.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.ServerCacheFallback
member.summary: A live fetch failed but a recent cached entry was served in its place, so `serverFetchFailed` stays false. Lets a consumer distinguish a clean fetch from a cache-backed fallback.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.ServerClientUpdateRequested
member.summary: Minimum client version requested by a successful response. Advisory only; the delivered policy remains active.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.ServerClientUpdateRequired
member.summary: The server refused to deliver a policy because this client is too old to enforce it, carrying the user-facing sentence describing the refusal. No retry will help; the remedy is a client update. Gates that exist only because of managed policy should deny on this rather than falling back to their unmanaged default.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.ServerFetchError
member.summary: The error that made the server fetch fail, when one did.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.ServerFetchFailed
member.summary: The server fetch failed and no cached entry stood in for it, so the server layer is unconfirmed and fail-closed gates apply.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.ServerForcedRefreshFailure
member.summary: The server fetch failed while a policy demanded a fresh confirmation, which is the strict posture an enterprise opted into rather than an ordinary transient failure.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.ServerPermissionsFloor
member.summary: The synthesized fail-closed permissions layer applied in place of a policy a refused client may not enforce.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.ServerResolution
member.summary: How the server layer was resolved.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.ServerResponse
member.summary: The account's server-delivered policy, when one was resolved.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.ServerRetryableFailure
member.summary: The server fetch failed in a way a later retry could succeed at, as opposed to a refusal that no retry will change.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.ServerSandboxFloor
member.summary: The sandbox object from a cached server policy that a forced refresh declined to serve in full. Folded back into the effective sandbox layer so an outage during a forced refresh still synthesizes the fail-closed sandbox floor from the administrator's known intent.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.ServerSourceFound
member.summary: A server-managed policy is known to exist even though `serverResponse` is intentionally unset. Consumers should OR this with the presence of `serverResponse` when deciding whether the device is managed, so a fresh start during an outage still applies the fail-closed gates instead of treating the device as unmanaged.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.ServerTokenUnavailable
member.summary: No usable token was available, so no server fetch was attempted.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestResult.Settings
member.summary: The effective managed settings composed from every resolved layer. Omitted when no layer set anything, so an unmanaged host locks nothing.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams
member.summary: Inputs describing the host and account an ingestion should resolve managed policy for.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.AuthInfo
member.summary: The authenticated identity to resolve policy for. Omitted before sign-in, in which case no server layer is fetched.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.BypassCacheRead
member.summary: Whether to ignore a cached server policy when reading, forcing the resolution to come from a live fetch.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.ClientName
member.summary: Name of the embedding client, reported to the managed-settings service as `client_id` so it can refuse to deliver a policy this client is too old to enforce. Omit it and the runtime reports a generic identity; the runtime version sent alongside is the gate that actually matters.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.DeviceResponse
member.summary: A device layer supplied by the host instead of discovered from the machine. Pair it with `hasDeviceResponse` so an explicit absence is distinguishable from an omitted override.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.Environment
member.summary: The host's environment variables, read for cache location and policy overrides. Supplied by the host rather than read from the runtime process so a command that selected its own configuration home is honored.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.HasDeviceResponse
member.summary: Whether `deviceResponse` is an override at all. True with a null `deviceResponse` asserts the device layer is empty; false discovers it from the machine.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.HomeDirectory
member.summary: The host's home directory, used to resolve cache and managed-file locations.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.Platform
member.summary: The host's platform, in Node's `process.platform` spelling, used to locate platform-specific cache and policy paths.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.PolicyHelperClientName

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.PolicyHelperEnabled
member.summary: Whether a configured platform policy helper may be run to produce an enforced helper layer.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.PolicyHelperReason
member.summary: The policy-helper invocation reason. Defaults to sessionStart.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.PolicyHelperWorkingDirectory
member.summary: Directory the policy helper runs in when this ingestion is not owned by a registered session. A host resolving policy before its session exists must pass this, or a directory-sensitive helper judges the wrong repository.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.SelfFetch

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.ServerPolicyCacheMode
member.summary: How this ingestion may use the on-disk server-policy cache. Defaults to the runtime's own policy when omitted.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.SessionId

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsIngestParams.UserAgent

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ForceLoginOrgsDecision
member.summary: The verdict of the `forceLoginOrgs` enterprise sign-in pin for one credential. A managed device may pin Copilot to an approved set of GitHub organizations so a developer cannot sign in with a personal — or another enterprise's — account and escape every control that keys off the signed-in identity. A host must refuse to proceed when `allowed` is false; the remaining fields explain the refusal rather than qualifying it.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ForceLoginOrgsDecision.Allowed
member.summary: Whether the client may proceed. True whenever no pin is in force, so an unmanaged host is never blocked.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ForceLoginOrgsDecision.Denial
member.summary: A stable kebab-case reason code when refused: `org-not-approved`, `unverifiable-credential`, `policy-undetermined`, `policy-invalid`, `not-signed-in`, or `membership-unknown`. Omitted when allowed. Treat an unrecognized code as a refusal rather than mapping it to an allow: a code this host has not been taught about still denied the credential.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ForceLoginOrgsDecision.Enforced
member.summary: Whether a pin applies at all. Distinguishes "allowed because unmanaged" from "allowed because the account is approved", which a diagnostics surface needs and which also decides whether a bring-your-own-key provider may serve inference.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ForceLoginOrgsDecision.MatchedOrg
member.summary: The approved organization the account matched, when allowed under a pin.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ForceLoginOrgsDecision.Message
member.summary: A developer-facing explanation of the refusal. Omitted when allowed.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ForceLoginOrgsDecision.PolicyDiagnostics
member.summary: Error-level detail from managed-policy discovery — which file failed to load, which field failed validation. Carried on the decision rather than left to the log because a refusal can exit the process before a log sink exists, which would discard the only actionable diagnostic a misconfigured managed device produces.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ForceLoginOrgsDecision.RequiredOrgs
member.summary: The approved organization logins, as configured. Enterprise configuration rather than user data, so it is safe to name in a message or a log line.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult
member.summary: The startup policy a resolution composed, the per-layer outcome flags a host needs to decide how much to trust it, and the enterprise sign-in verdict for the credential it ran against. The flags are reported rather than folded into the settings because a host must distinguish an unmanaged device from a managed device whose policy could not be confirmed, and apply its fail-closed gates in the second case.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.ClientUpdateRequested
member.summary: Advisory minimum client version from a successful server response.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.ClientUpdateRequired
member.summary: The server refused to deliver a policy because this client is too old to enforce it, carrying the user-facing sentence describing the refusal. No retry will help; the remedy is a client update.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.DeviceLoadFailed
member.summary: The device layer could not be read, so it is unconfirmed rather than known-absent.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.DeviceResponse
member.summary: The device layer discovered from the machine, when one exists.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.DeviceSandboxFloor
member.summary: The sandbox floor contributed by the device layer.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.ForceLoginOrgs
member.summary: The enterprise sign-in verdict for the credential this resolution ran against, evaluated over the effective policy so a server-delivered pin is honored alongside a device one. Computed on every resolution, including one that was not retained, so a host that declines to apply policy still cannot proceed past a pin.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.ManagedPolicyPresent
member.summary: A managed policy is known to apply to this host, from a discovered source or a resolved document.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.PermissionPolicyUndetermined
member.summary: The permissions layer specifically could not be confirmed, so permission gates apply their fail-closed posture.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.PolicyHelperFailure
member.summary: Structured latest Policy Helper failure for this startup resolution, when one occurred.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.PolicyHelperLoadFailed
member.summary: The policy helper was configured but could not be run, or its output could not be read.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.PolicyHelperResponse
member.summary: The layer produced by the platform policy helper, when one ran.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.PolicyUndetermined
member.summary: Some layer of the policy could not be confirmed, so its absence must not be read as permission. Folds in a failed server fetch as well as an unreadable device layer.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.SandboxEnabledByUndeterminedPolicy
member.summary: The sandbox was enabled because policy could not be confirmed rather than because an administrator asked for it. Lets a host explain a sandbox the user did not configure.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.SandboxFloor
member.summary: The effective sandbox floor composed across every layer, which a host must apply rather than its own default.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.ServerFetchFailed
member.summary: The server fetch failed and no cached entry stood in for it, so the server layer is unconfirmed and fail-closed gates apply.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.ServerResponse

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyResult.Telemetry

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyParams.BypassCacheRead
member.summary: Whether to ignore a cached server policy when reading, forcing the resolution to come from a live fetch.

member.summary: Name of the embedding client, reported to the managed-settings service as `client_id` so it can refuse to deliver a policy this client is too old to enforce.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyParams.DeviceResponse

member.summary: Caller identity for a policy helper before session registration. Omit to keep the runtime default. This does not change clientName on managed-service requests.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyParams.PolicyHelperEnabled
member.summary: Whether a configured platform policy helper may be run to produce an enforced helper layer.

member.summary: The policy-helper invocation reason. Defaults to sessionStart.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyParams.PolicyHelperWorkingDirectory
member.summary: Directory the policy helper runs in when this resolution is not owned by a registered session. A host resolving policy before its session exists must pass this, or a directory-sensitive helper judges the wrong repository.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyParams.RetainAndApply
member.summary: Whether to retain the resolved policy as this runtime process's startup policy, so later work in the process enforces it. Set false to resolve without side effects, which is what a protocol host wants before session creation: its sessions apply the complete policy through the normal lifecycle, and retaining here would let a readiness credential affect unrelated sessions. The returned verdict is identical either way — this decides only whether the process keeps it.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyParams.SelfFetch
member.summary: Whether to run ingestion. Omit or set false to return an empty result without discovering or fetching policy.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyParams.ServerPolicyCacheMode
member.summary: How this resolution may use the on-disk server-policy cache. Defaults to the runtime's own policy when omitted. Rejected when combined with `bypassCacheRead`, because the two express the same decision and accepting both would leave the caller unsure which one the runtime honored.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyParams.SessionId
member.summary: The session whose credential store, working directory and client kind the resolution should use. Omit it when no session exists yet and the process-wide store applies. A resolution whose session names a credential other than `authInfo` is returned but not retained, so a stale sign-in cannot apply policy for an account that has already been switched away from.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolveStartupPolicyParams.UserAgent
member.summary: User agent to send with the policy fetch.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsLoadRemoteControlResult
member.summary: The managed remote-control policy in force for an account, if any. An absent policy means the account is unmanaged for this capability, which a host reads as allowed — so absence here is a positive statement that no policy applies, never a stand-in for a resolution that failed. A resolution that cannot be completed is rejected instead.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsLoadRemoteControlResult.RemoteControl
member.summary: The account's `remoteControl` policy document. Absent when no managed policy governs remote control for this account. Reported as an explicit disabled policy, rather than as absence, when the service refused to deliver a policy this client is too old to enforce.

That refusal is exactly what turns into an explicit `disabled` below, so a host that omits this field forfeits the protection.

member.summary: The host's environment variables, read for cache location and policy overrides.

member.summary: The host's environment variables. Read for the variables that would make an identity's membership snapshot forgeable, so a credential whose provenance cannot be trusted is refused rather than accepted.

member.summary: Resolve the current credential from this connection's original auth owner only when device policy enforces a pin. Refreshes membership and preserves credential-resolution diagnostics. Defaults to false, which evaluates authInfo as supplied. Cannot be combined with authInfo; requires an original auth-owner binding.

member.summary: Channel identifier: `device` (MDM, plist, registry, or managed file), `server` (account or organization policy), or `policyHelper` (session-local helper output, supported by compose). Treat unknown output values as additional channels; more may be added.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolvedData
member.summary: Effective enterprise managed settings and contributing channels. Session events report applied policy; sessionless resolve reports an account/device snapshot, and compose reports a non-applying preview of candidate documents. Device values take precedence over server values, then the policy helper, per ordinary key, while permissions compose restrictively. Session-local SDK-client policy is included only in session results. Marked experimental while the managed-settings surface stabilizes.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolvedData.BypassPermissionsDisabled
member.summary: Whether an explicit enterprise policy restriction disables bypass-permissions ("yolo") mode for this session. Deny-wins across layers; an unresolved policy does not force this on by itself.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolvedData.ClientManaged
member.summary: Whether a session-local permissions layer injected by the SDK host was present.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolvedData.DeviceManaged
member.summary: Whether an actual device MDM/plist/registry/file managed-settings layer was present.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolvedData.FailClosed
member.summary: Whether managed policy could not be determined (e.g. a failed server fetch) and unresolved-policy safeguards remain active. This does not by itself disable bypass-permissions; `bypassPermissionsDisabled` reports only an explicit policy restriction.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolvedData.ManagedKeys
member.summary: The setting keys under enterprise management in the effective managed settings (e.g. `model`, `enabledPlugins`, `permissions`). Empty when no managed settings are in force.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolvedData.PermissionsAllowIntersected
member.summary: Whether at least two managed sources supplied permission allowlists, so enforcement intersects them and the flattened settings payload omits `permissions.allow`.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolvedData.PermissionsContext
member.summary: Reusable retained managed permission policy for managedSettings.permissions.evaluate, including source composition and session-local injection. Provided by live session snapshots; absent in older events. Refresh the context when managed policy changes.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolvedData.PolicyHelperCapabilities
member.summary: Explicit Policy Helper structured-failure and recheck capabilities supported by this runtime.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolvedData.PolicyHelperFailure
member.summary: The latest unresolved Policy Helper failure for this exact policy context. It remains present across retained-policy refresh failures and clears only after fresh success or authoritative removal.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolvedData.PolicyHelperManaged
member.summary: Whether the policy-helper managed-settings layer was present. The policy helper is the weakest channel: it fills keys no enterprise source set and can never replace one.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsResolvedData.SandboxEnabledByUndeterminedPolicy
member.summary: Whether the effective sandbox policy forces the sandbox on *only* because managed policy could not be determined, rather than because the policy requires it. Lets clients tell a user whose `--no-sandbox` was overridden that the sandbox stayed on as a fail-closed fallback, instead of attributing it to an administrator who set no such policy.

Absent on runtimes that do not support permission evaluation.

member.summary: Typed effective values of managed settings, keyed like the managed-settings schema and already resolved across channels, with the `{ "overridable": ... }` wrapper removed. Present when policy sets at least one typed key. Keys not typed here are available in `resolved.settings`.

member.summary: One candidate channel; absent settings represents a channel that delivered no document.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsComposeLayer.Settings
member.summary: Candidate managed-settings document. Omit when the channel delivered none, as in resolve output.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsComposeLayer.Source
member.summary: The channel whose candidate document is being supplied.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsComposeRequest
member.summary: Candidate managed-settings documents to merge without applying them.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ManagedSettingsComposeRequest.Layers
member.summary: One entry per channel. `source` must be `device`, `server`, or `policyHelper`, each at most once (checked at runtime); order does not matter, because channel precedence is fixed. To preview documents from resolve output, map recognized source strings to ManagedSettingsChannel and copy their settings; generated resolve and compose layer types are distinct. Omitted settings means this channel delivered no document. Supplied documents must be valid within the preview limits; warnings are returned in diagnostics. Compose does not reproduce source-failure state or retained enforcement floors from resolve.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.DiscoveredHook
member.summary: One server-discovered hook action from user, repository, plugin, or managed-policy configuration.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.DiscoveredHook.DefinitionFileUri
member.summary: File URI of the document defining this action on the selected runtime host, not the command or script it executes. Inline hooks point to their containing settings document or plugin manifest. Omitted for sources without a backing file, such as registry policy.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.DiscoveredHook.DisableKey
member.summary: Durable content hash used by hook enablement. Identical actions may intentionally share this key. Omitted when changing the user's disabled-hooks setting cannot change the action's current server-discovered state, including managed-policy hooks, session-start prompt actions, actions suppressed by disable-all settings, and projectless plugin actions that require project-directory expansion.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.DiscoveredHook.Enabled
member.summary: Whether this action is enabled under the server-side discovery settings. Concrete sessions may differ because they can add session-specific directories, plugins, or trust. False when its disable key is present in the user's disabled-hooks setting or disable-all settings suppress the action.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.DiscoveredHook.HookType
member.summary: Hook event that invokes this action.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.DiscoveredHook.Id
member.summary: Deterministic identifier for this server-discovered action row. It remains stable while the project, origin, source, event, action content, and duplicate ordinal are unchanged. This is row identity, not the key persisted in disabledHooks.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.DiscoveredHook.Origin
member.summary: Configuration tier that contributed this hook action.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.DiscoveredHook.PluginId
member.summary: Opaque identity of the plugin owning this action. Matches plugins.list().plugins[].id and MCP effectiveSource.plugin.id on the same runtime host. Compare the complete value without parsing it. Omitted for non-plugin hooks.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.DiscoveredHook.ProjectPath
member.summary: Input project path for which this server-side action was resolved. Set on every row returned for project-scoped discovery, including repeated user and policy actions.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.DiscoveredHook.Source
member.summary: Human-readable source label, such as a hook file path, settings source, or plugin name.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HooksDiscoverResult
member.summary: Server-discovered hook actions and partial-load diagnostics from user, repository, plugin, and managed-policy sources. Concrete sessions may include additional session-specific hook sources.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HooksDiscoverResult.Errors
member.summary: Errors for hook sources or actions that could not be loaded, making the result partially incomplete. Other valid actions are still returned. Project-resolution and repository-settings errors are prefixed with their project path.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HooksDiscoverResult.Hooks
member.summary: All discovered hook actions. Byte-identical actions remain separate rows even when they share a disable key.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HooksDiscoverResult.Warnings
member.summary: Non-fatal source-loading warnings. Discovery remains complete for the affected source, although the source had a recoverable issue. Repository-settings warnings are prefixed with their project path when attribution is available.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HooksDiscoverRequest
member.summary: Optional project paths and host-exclusion behavior for server-scoped hook discovery.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HooksDiscoverRequest.ExcludeHostHooks
member.summary: When true, omit host-owned user and plugin hook rows and their diagnostics. Managed-policy hooks and trusted repository hooks remain visible, and host disabledHooks still contribute to each remaining row's effective enabled state. This filters sources rather than simulating a host with no settings.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HooksDiscoverRequest.HookDirectories
member.summary: Explicit discovery-only file-hook roots, separate from callback hooks and filesystem grants. Available without ambient discovery or repository file-hook enablement, subject to managed/hook disables. Relative paths resolve against the request's effective working directory when supplied. Null and omission are equivalent; an empty array contributes no explicit roots.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HooksDiscoverRequest.ProjectPaths
member.summary: Optional project directory paths whose trusted repository and project-expanded plugin hooks should be discovered. When omitted or empty, user, managed-policy, and globally enabled installed or explicit plugin hooks are returned without project expansion.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.Model.Provider
member.summary: The native model provider that produced this model, as a neutral reference (opaque id, human-readable label, and provider kind). Preserved by `session.model.list` and `server.models.list` when supplied by the catalog producer; omitted for unattributed and configured BYOK models. This identifies the model source, not an account or agent harness.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.Model.SupportedContextTiers
member.summary: Context-window tiers this model offers, when the provider advertises them independently of tiered token pricing. Copilot models carry their tiers in `billing.tokenPrices`; a provider that has no pricing to publish (an agent host reached over AHP, for example) declares them here instead, so the model picker can still offer the tier toggle.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.Model.SupportedReasoningEfforts

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.Model.Vendor
member.summary: Model vendor as the Copilot API reports it, for example "Anthropic" or "Azure OpenAI". Open vocabulary, passed through unchanged. It can name the vendor that serves the model instead of the one that built it, or a label that is not a vendor, such as "Experimental". Absent when the Copilot API reports no vendor.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.Model.WarningMessages

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.Model.WarningText

member.summary: The protocol version and capability set a caller requires, supplied on every catalog request so negotiation cannot be skipped by omission.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogClientContract.ProtocolVersion
member.summary: SDK protocol version the caller was generated against. A caller below the runtime's minimum supported version is refused rather than served a partial result.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogClientContract.RequiredCapabilities
member.summary: Wire features the caller requires the runtime to understand. Identifiers are bounded but extensible so a newer caller can negotiate with an older runtime. Requiring an unknown feature yields a typed refusal listing what is understood, never a partial grant. A grant does not promise that a deployment has enabled the operation; typed unavailable results report that separately.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpPlanInstallSourceCandidate.SearchId
member.summary: The runtime- or authority-minted `searchId` returned with the search that produced this candidate. Planning verifies the private correlation and atomically consumes a matching candidate before downstream work, including attempts that subsequently fail or report unavailable. A mismatched search does not consume the candidate. It identifies a search rather than a person and must never be joined with user identity to re-identify anyone.

member.summary: The credential the search runs under, carried opaquely. Hosts usually send credential-free `AuthIdentity`; a `token` identity can be resolved only when it embeds a token, while `env` and `gh-cli` identities can use a token embedded in the request first.

member.summary: Repository used for the policy lookup, as `owner/name`. The policy selects the registry URL and whether the user token goes to the registry. The registry receives this repository only when the policy entry lists it as required context. A value that is not a string is refused.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpRegistrySearchRequest.RequestId
member.summary: Request ID from `mcp.registry.allocateRequestId`. The search refuses unknown, reclaimed, or canceled IDs and IDs that another search or request already uses.

member.summary: Description from the manifest of the installed copy. Present only for a direct install pinned to one GitHub commit, such as a verified install from GitHub.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.InstalledPluginInfo.DirectSourceId
member.summary: Opaque, stable hash identifying a direct (non-marketplace) install source. Present only for direct repo / URL / local installs; absent for marketplace plugins. Same source yields the same id; distinct sources never collide.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.InstalledPluginInfo.Enabled
member.summary: Whether the plugin is currently enabled for new sessions.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.InstalledPluginInfo.IconUrl
member.summary: HTTPS URL of the plugin's icon on raw.githubusercontent.com, retained from the catalogue entry it was installed from. Untrusted external content: load it without credentials. Present only for a direct install pinned to one GitHub commit whose catalogue entry had an icon.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.InstalledPluginInfo.Id
member.summary: Opaque plugin identity in this runtime's inventory. Matches MCP effectiveSource.plugin.id for the same plugin. Stable across enablement changes, updates and restarts while the installation source is unchanged; not a cross-host identifier or a mutation argument. Compare the complete value without parsing it. May be absent on older runtimes.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.InstalledPluginInfo.Installed
member.summary: Whether the managed desired plugin currently has an installed or live record. Set to false for a managed desired entry retained in the listing after installation or reconciliation failed.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.InstalledPluginInfo.InstalledFrom
member.summary: Absolute path of the marketplace directory a live plugin was resolved from. Present only on live, never-persisted records — a plugin belonging to a directory/local marketplace, which is loaded from its real directory on every pass instead of a copy under the installed-plugins cache. Its presence is what marks a listed plugin as live: such a plugin is always present on disk, so `enabled` is its only meaningful state and it is never "not installed".

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.InstalledPluginInfo.Managed
member.summary: Whether enterprise managed settings control this plugin's enabled state.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.InstalledPluginInfo.ManagedDesiredEnabled
member.summary: The enabled state required by enterprise managed settings, when this plugin spec is managed.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.PluginInstallResult.Warnings
member.summary: Report-and-ignore warnings raised while reading the plugin's manifest, such as a field the manifest's schema does not define and the loader therefore ignored. Callers should surface these to end users: a plugin whose skills sit behind an ignored field otherwise installs, lists, and contributes nothing, with no signal to its author. Absent when the manifest raised none.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.PluginsEnableRequest
member.summary: Plugin names (or specs) to enable, plus the optional working directory the repository-controlled guard is evaluated against.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.PluginsEnableRequest.Names
member.summary: Plugin names, "plugin@marketplace" specs, or opaque directSourceId values from inventory to enable. Use directSourceId to distinguish same-named direct installations. Unknown targets and session-only plugin-directory mounts are ignored. Direct-install decisions persist on the installation record; active sessions must reload plugins to load newly enabled contributions.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.PluginsEnableRequest.WorkingDirectory
member.summary: Working directory whose repository `enabledPlugins` overlay decides whether this mutation is repository-controlled. Hosts that serve sessions across several repositories (the SDK server) should pass the session's directory; otherwise the guard is evaluated against the server process's own working directory, which may belong to a different repository. Defaults to the server's current working directory.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.PluginsDisableRequest
member.summary: Plugin names (or specs) to disable, plus the optional working directory the repository-controlled guard is evaluated against.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.PluginsDisableRequest.Names
member.summary: Plugin names, "plugin@marketplace" specs, or opaque directSourceId values from inventory to disable. Use directSourceId to distinguish same-named direct installations. Unknown targets and session-only plugin-directory mounts are ignored. Direct-install decisions persist on the installation record. Plugin-owned MCP servers are stopped in active sessions immediately; other plugin contributions remain available until each session reloads plugins.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.PluginsDisableRequest.WorkingDirectory
member.summary: Working directory whose repository `enabledPlugins` overlay decides whether this mutation is repository-controlled. Hosts that serve sessions across several repositories (the SDK server) should pass the session's directory; otherwise the guard is evaluated against the server process's own working directory, which may belong to a different repository. Defaults to the server's current working directory.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogPluginRepositorySource.Repository
member.summary: Canonical lowercase owner/repository name derived from metadata.sourceSet.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin
member.summary: An inert Agent Plugin catalog result. Its canonical catalog identity, declared version, repository source claim, and explicit compatibility tags are safe to correlate, while its descriptor, URL, raw data, materialisation reference, and installed-plugin state remain runtime-private. A handle is minted only under agent-plugin-confirmed-installation, for a candidate with a complete materialisation reference.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.Categories
member.summary: Category slugs reported by the feed, such as `build` or `review`, without repeats. Values are passed through, so clients must tolerate slugs they do not recognise. Inert untrusted text. Omitted when the feed reports none.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.CompatibilityTags
member.summary: Explicit validated compatibility tags, in canonical order. An empty list means the source declared no recognised compatibility; clients must not infer compatibility from other fields. `canvas-only` requires both `canvas` and `github-copilot`.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.ConnectorIds
member.summary: Identifiers of the connectors the resource works with, as reported by the feed, without repeats. Inert untrusted text. Omitted when the feed reports none.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.Description
member.summary: Description taken verbatim from the card. Inert untrusted text.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.DisplayName
member.summary: Display name taken verbatim from the card. Inert untrusted text.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.Handle
member.summary: Opaque, runtime-instance scoped, TTL-bound, single-use handle for planning this plugin's installation through plugins.planInstall. Present only when the caller requires the agent-plugin-confirmed-installation capability and the candidate carries a complete Agent Finder materialisation reference, which stays runtime-private. Never logged.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.HandleExpiresAt
member.summary: ISO 8601 timestamp after which the handle is stale and will be rejected. Present exactly when handle is present.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.IconUrl
member.summary: HTTPS URL of the resource's icon on raw.githubusercontent.com, as reported by the feed. Untrusted external content: load it without credentials. Omitted when absent or outside the feed's icon host policy.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.Identity
member.summary: Validated, normalised catalogue resource URN. This identity comes only from the catalog identifier and is never inferred from display text or installed-plugin state.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.Installability
member.summary: Whether this plugin can be installed in the selected session. Present only when the caller requires the agent-plugin-confirmed-installation capability.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.InstallCount
member.summary: How many times the resource has been installed, as reported by the feed. Omitted when the feed reports no count or an invalid one.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.InstallPlan
member.summary: Reviewable install plan built only from verified catalogue install data. Present exactly when installability is `installable`; the runtime never derives it from the repository source, display text, or identity.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.MediaType
member.summary: Media type naming the plugin's format.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.Provenance
member.summary: Where the Agent Plugin catalog reference was observed, without its descriptor, URL, raw data, or content digest.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.Publisher
member.summary: Publisher taken verbatim from the card. Inert untrusted text.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.Source
member.summary: Bounded repository provenance declared through the catalog's sourceSet and repoPath metadata. It contains no descriptor URL. Always present, with a path, unless the caller requires agent-plugin-confirmed-installation. Such a caller also receives a repository-root plugin (sourceSet without repoPath) whose source has no path, and a plugin with no usable declaration (neither key, or repoPath alone) and no source; the latter carries a complete materialisation reference and a handle, and the verified descriptor supplies the repository, commit and root when it is planned. Never derived from the catalogue URL.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.Trust
member.summary: Versioned trust metadata observed from the catalog authority. Optional for protocol-3 compatibility and emitted only when the caller also requires the trust-snapshot capability.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCandidatePlugin.Version
member.summary: Optional version declared by the catalog source. Omitted rather than guessed when the source supplies no version.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogSearchPagination.MaxPage

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogSearchPagination.PageCount
member.summary: Backend-reported page count, which may exceed maxPage. Present pagination metadata always describes a multi-page result; zero- and single-page responses omit pagination. Navigation targets must also be within the signed pageCount carried by the supplied token.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogSearchPagination.PageSize

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogSearchPagination.Token

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogSearchPagination.TotalCountRelation

member.summary: Matching candidates, never more than the requested limit. All text is inert untrusted data.

member.summary: Protocol version and capabilities the runtime honoured.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogSearchResultSucceeded.Pagination

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogSearchResultSucceeded.SearchId
member.summary: Pseudonymous identifier for this search, issued by the runtime or by the catalog authority it queried and never by the caller, so it cannot be forged or replayed to attribute an install to a search that never happened.
