member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CapiSessionOptions.AutoTier
member.summary: Routing preference for sessions whose model is `auto`. On create or cold resume, this establishes the preference sent as `tier` on CAPI `/auto` requests; when omitted on cold resume, the runtime restores the last committed preference. On resident resume, a different value requests a safe switch after resume succeeds and cannot change an in-flight turn. Successful switches are persisted for later cold resume. When no preference is supplied or restored, CAPI default routing is used. `fast` is an integrator-only latency preset, not a first-party GitHub Copilot product preference.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CapiSessionOptions.EnableWebSocketResponses
member.summary: Whether to use WebSocket transport for the CAPI Responses API. Enabled by default when the model advertises `ws:/responses` support; set to `false` to force the HTTP Responses transport in environments where WebSockets are blocked (e.g. behind a proxy). Setting this to `false` is equivalent to the `COPILOT_CLI_DISABLE_WEBSOCKET_RESPONSES` environment variable.

member.summary: When true, prevents Assisted Permissions from being activated. An actively Assisted session falls back to Manual Approval while the policy is in force. Omit the key or set it to false to impose no restriction.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionManagedPermissions.DisableBypassPermissionsMode
member.summary: When set to `disable`, prevents bypass/allow-all permission modes. Advisory auto-approval remains available because normal prompt paths stay active. Any other value is accepted rather than failing the session, but is enforced as `disable`: the key is only present to restrict something, so a mode this runtime cannot interpret fails closed to the most restrictive one it knows. Omit the key entirely to impose no restriction.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionManagedPermissions.LimitTo
member.summary: Closed-world host boundary expressed as `Domain(hostname)`, `Domain(IP)`, or `Domain(*.example.com)` rules. Schemes, ports, paths, queries, and fragments are rejected because every network request must be enforceable at host-level egress. Multiple managed sources intersect their lists; an empty list denies all hosts.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ShellCredentials
member.summary:
Command-scoped GitHub credential injection for the shell commands an agent runs.
Each channel is opt-in and independent, and injection is scoped to the individual command spawn: the credential is resolved from the session's *current* authentication at every spawn and reaches only spawns whose script actually invokes `git` or `gh`. Because nothing is retained between spawns, replacing the session credential (`session.gitHubAuth.setCredentials`) changes what the next spawned command presents — which seeding a credential into the runtime process's own environment cannot do, since a child's environment is fixed at `exec`.
The credential is matched to the host it authenticates to, so a github.com credential is never presented to a GitHub Enterprise host and vice versa. Where a channel cannot express that boundary it injects nothing rather than crossing it -- see `gh` below.
This is independent of `sandboxConfig`: it is a decision about which identity the agent presents, not about what the agent may touch, and it works on every platform whether or not an OS sandboxing backend is available. `sandboxConfig.auth` remains the sandbox-scoped spelling and is additive with this one.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ShellCredentials.Gh
member.summary:
Whether to authenticate the agent's `gh` commands as the session's GitHub credential, by exporting `GH_TOKEN` to a spawn that runs `gh`. Any inherited `gh` credential is removed from spawns that do not, so the credential stays command-scoped.
Applies to a github.com credential only. `gh` picks its credential variable from the host a command targets rather than the one the credential belongs to, and the command can choose that target, so `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN` would offer a single-tenant enterprise credential to every other enterprise host. A session whose credential is enterprise-scoped therefore runs `gh` unauthenticated; its `git` commands are unaffected, because `http.<host>.extraheader` is scoped to one host by construction. Default: false (opt-in).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ShellCredentials.Git
member.summary: Whether to authenticate the agent's `git` commands as the session's GitHub credential, by injecting an `http.<host>.extraheader` (plus `insteadOf` rewrites so SSH-spelled remotes for that host use the authenticated HTTPS transport). Applied only to a spawn that runs a remote-contacting `git` subcommand. Default: false (opt-in).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ShellOptions.InitScripts
member.summary: Ordered host-provided script paths sourced before each built-in shell command when the entry's shell target matches the active shell. Use these for rc files, environment setup scripts, or other custom scripts. A script that returns a nonzero status is reported, and later scripts and the user command continue while the shell remains running. Because scripts are sourced into the command shell, `exit`, `exec`, failures under `set -e`, or other shell-terminating behavior can prevent continuation. Script standard output is preserved; Bash script stderr is discarded, PowerShell exception messages are replaced, and runtime-generated failure notices omit configured script paths. When sandboxing is enabled, each script must already be readable under the active sandbox filesystem policy. Pass an empty array to clear the list.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionOpenOptions.AdditionalDirectories
member.summary: Additional directories the agent may access beyond the working directory. Each entry is granted to the session's file-access allow-list and surfaced to the model (system prompt context and `@`-mention completion). Conventional `.github/skills/` and `.github/agents/` definitions under each directory also join the session's project catalogs when their existing subsystem gates are enabled: added-root skills require both `enableConfigDiscovery` and effective `enableSkills`; added-root agents require `enableConfigDiscovery`. Supplying a directory therefore activates configuration from it and should be treated as a trust decision. Absolute paths are recommended; a relative path is resolved against the session's working directory. Nonexistent or unresolvable entries are skipped with a warning. This is applied during session creation and cold resume and is not persisted, so a cold resume must re-supply the directories.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionOpenOptions.EnableFileChangeTracking
member.summary: Opt in to capturing file changes for session rewind and session diff. Capture cannot reconstruct changes made before it was enabled. On create it starts capture from the first turn. It is also honored on resume: for a session that already has tracked prior turns, tracking continues automatically even if this is omitted; passing it on resume additionally enables tracking for an eligible session that has no prior root turn yet. Resuming a session whose prior root turns were never tracked has no restorable baseline, so tracking stays disabled for it and rewind reports file change tracking as unavailable; the resume itself still succeeds, so sessions that predate tracking remain loadable. The opt-in is only rejected when the session can never track (a subagent session, or one without local session storage). It is intentionally absent from the mutable options update because enabling it after edits have occurred would create an incomplete, misleading baseline. Subagents share the parent session's capture store and are not tracked as separate rewind points: a file a subagent writes is attributed to whichever root user turn was open when the capture was staged, just before the tool body ran. A turn cannot open while a staged capture is still in flight, so a subagent tool that staged under the spawning turn stays attributed to it however late the write lands, while a capture it stages after the user's next message belongs to that later turn. Attribution decides which turn's rewind point counts and file preview include that write; it does not narrow which rewinds revert it, because a rewind restores every capture from the selected turn onward, so the earlier spawning turn reverts it as well.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionOpenOptions.EnableFileHooks
member.summary: Live gate for repository-origin file hooks, including the primary repository, trusted repository-configured roots, and accepted startup additional directories (including CLI --add-dir). False suppresses these hooks; explicit hookDirectories and SDK callbacks are independent. Additional-root eligibility and the DISABLE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORY_HOOKS escape hatch are captured at create/cold resume, not expanded by later grants or feature-flag changes. Discovery uses containing Git roots, so supply only trusted repositories: commands and prompts need no further approval. Policy, hook-disable settings, and sandbox rules still apply. Provider-backed sessions skip repository hooks with a warning on omission, skip silently on false, and reject explicit true.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventsReadResult
member.summary: Batch of session events returned by a read, with cursor and continuation metadata.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventsReadResult.Cursor
member.summary: Opaque cursor for the next read. Pass back unchanged in the next read.cursor to continue from where this read left off. Always present, even when no events were returned. For a backward read this cursor pages toward OLDER events; keep passing `direction: backward` with it (the cursor is also self-describing, so backward paging continues correctly).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventsReadResult.CursorStatus
member.summary: Cursor status: 'ok' means the cursor was applied successfully. For session.eventLog.read, 'expired' means the cursor referred to an event that no longer exists in active history and the read fell back to a boundary of the remaining history: the beginning for a forward read or the newest window for a backward read. That fallback may overlap already rendered events, so active-session consumers should reset, rebase, or deduplicate before continuing. sessions.readPersistedEvents has stricter snapshot semantics: 'expired' returns an empty terminal page and never switches to a replacement journal generation. Other persisted-read I/O failures are RPC errors with diagnostics, not cursor expiry.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventsReadResult.Events
member.summary: Session events for this batch, merged into a single stream in creation order: durable (persisted) events and ephemeral events interleave exactly as they were emitted. Set `includeEphemeral: false` to receive only durable events. Ephemeral events are never replayable once pruned from the in-memory ring, so a consumer that needs them should keep reading with a non-zero `waitMs`. For a backward (tail-first) read, the returned window contains persisted events only, still in chronological (oldest-to-newest) append order.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventsReadResult.HasMore
member.summary: True when more events are available in the read's direction. For a backward read, true means older persisted events remain before the returned window. A persisted-event page may contain fewer than `max` events because of its byte budget while still reporting hasMore true; continue according to this flag rather than the event count.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionsReadPersistedEventsRequest
member.summary: Pagination options for reading an inactive or active local session's persisted event journal.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionsReadPersistedEventsRequest.Cursor
member.summary: Opaque, process-local, single-use cursor returned by the previous persisted-event read. Omit on the first call and issue continuations sequentially; reusing the same cursor returns an expired terminal page.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionsReadPersistedEventsRequest.Direction
member.summary: Direction to page through persisted history. Forward starts at the beginning; backward starts with the newest events. Events in each page remain chronological. This selects the initial read only; a continuation always uses the direction bound into its cursor.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionsReadPersistedEventsRequest.Max
member.summary: Maximum number of events to return in this batch (1–1000, default 200). Pages may contain fewer events to keep the serialized event array within a soft 1 MiB budget including resolved binary assets; one oversized event is returned alone to guarantee progress.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionsReadPersistedEventsRequest.SessionId

Model-derived classifications can be inaccurate or manipulated by adversarial content. member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TaskAnalyticsClassifyTrajectoryRequest
member.summary: Retrospectively classify a recorded Copilot or ATIF trajectory without a conversation session. Explicitly requests model processing through the connection's GitHub CAPI credentials, independently of background telemetry consent, not through BYOK endpoints. Callers must be authorized to send the supplied content for analysis. Does not execute archived tools, append conversation history, or emit classification telemetry.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TaskAnalyticsClassifyTrajectoryRequest.Classifiers
member.summary: Classifier names to run. Omit for all eight classifiers. An empty list runs none. Turn splitting is also returned when needed to build task/session units or identify task-opening turns.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TaskAnalyticsClassifyTrajectoryRequest.Events
member.summary: Canonical Copilot session event objects or ATIF step objects, in source order, starting at the beginning of the recorded conversation. An ATIF document containing steps can be passed as a single array element. Include source identifiers when present. Durable Copilot logs are accepted; abort events retain interruptions, and EOF closes an unfinished turn without claiming successful completion. Non-analytics event types are ignored. Treat the archive as untrusted input: this API does not authenticate its origin, roles, completion claims, or content. Callers must validate provenance and preserve event structure, ordering, and role/source metadata. Remove or redact secrets and personal data that must not be sent to GitHub CAPI before calling; automatic redaction and prompt-injection sanitization are not provided. Retained text is bounded, not made trustworthy. Adversarial instructions can bias model judgments just as in live conversations; stripping instruction-like text is not required and can change the evidence being measured.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TaskAnalyticsClassifyTrajectoryRequest.Judge
member.summary: Explicit judge configuration for this analysis. Omit to use each classifier's production model policy and reasoning effort. The exact model must be offered by the authenticated catalog, allowed by server policy, and compatible with the classifier; an unusable override fails the affected classification rather than falling back. Choosing a billed model explicitly authorizes its inference costs. Successful rows reused from previousResult keep their original judge configuration.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TaskAnalyticsClassifyTrajectoryRequest.MaxConcurrentRequests
member.summary: Maximum concurrent classifier calls in this analysis across all lanes, including segmentation and session classifiers. Defaults to 4; must be positive. Multiple simultaneous analyses each have their own limit. Trajectory concurrency is not inference-request concurrency.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TaskAnalyticsClassifyTrajectoryRequest.PreviousResult
member.summary: Previous result for the identical archive and classifier versions. Reuses all original task boundaries, including unresolved ones, and preserves successful and declined outcomes. Only failed/abandoned non-segmenting outcomes in the selected classifiers are retried. Start a fresh analysis to change segmentation. Rejects mismatched fingerprints or versions before inference.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TaskAnalyticsClassifyTrajectoryRequest.ValidateOnly
member.summary: Validate input locally without authentication, model discovery, or inference. Returns validation diagnostics and no classifications. Invalid input never starts paid inference, even when this option is omitted.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CloudTasksCreateResult
member.summary: The outcome of starting a cloud task. A rejected request and a failed one are reported separately: `reason` and `message` describe a request the service declined, while `statusCode` and `errorMessage` describe the HTTP call itself and appear only when one was actually made.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CloudTasksCreateResult.ErrorMessage
member.summary: Human-readable explanation of a failed HTTP call, when one failed.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CloudTasksCreateResult.ErrorPayloadJson
member.summary: The error body the service returned, preserved verbatim so a host can surface the service's own message.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CloudTasksCreateResult.Message
member.summary: The explanation to show for a declined request, when the service supplied one. This describes the rejection itself, unlike `errorMessage`, which describes a failed HTTP call.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CloudTasksCreateResult.Ok
member.summary: Whether the task was created.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CloudTasksCreateResult.Reason
member.summary: Why the request was declined, when it was. Carried as a free-form string rather than a fixed set because the vocabulary is the service's and grows with it; `policy_blocked`, `validation`, `rate_limited` and `error` are the values seen so far, and a caller should treat an unrecognised one as a generic failure rather than rejecting the response.

member.summary: Parameters for sending a user message to the session.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.AgentMode
member.summary: The UI mode the agent was in when this message was sent. Defaults to the session's current mode.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.Attachments
member.summary: Optional attachments (files, directories, selections, blobs, GitHub references) to include with the message.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.Billable
member.summary: If false, this message will not trigger a Premium Request Unit charge. User messages default to billable.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.ClientTurnId
member.summary: Opaque caller-chosen ID for the turn this message starts. The runtime copies it unchanged into `params._meta["com.github.copilot/turnId"]` on every MCP `tools/call` the agent makes while serving that turn, including calls from sub-agents it spawns and from Autopilot continuations of it. Visible user steering (`mode: "immediate"`) that a running turn consumes hands it to a successor turn: the steering's value replaces the running turn's from the next model call onward, and steering without one clears it. System and hidden steering leave it unchanged. A turn started without one, including one the runtime starts itself, carries no turn ID. The `user.message` event for each message the send delivers echoes it as `clientTurnId` when the message is consumed, and is persisted like other events; the value stamped on MCP calls is held in memory only and is not restored on resume.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.DisplayPrompt
member.summary: If provided, this is shown in the timeline instead of `prompt`.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.Mode
member.summary: How to deliver the message. `enqueue` (default) appends to the message queue. `immediate` interjects during an in-progress turn.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.Prepend
member.summary: If true, adds the message to the front of the queue instead of the end.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.Prompt
member.summary: The user message text.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.RequestHeaders
member.summary: Custom HTTP headers to include in outbound model requests for this turn. Merged with session-level provider headers; per-turn headers augment and overwrite session-level headers with the same key.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.RequiredTool
member.summary: If set, the request will fail if the named tool is not available when this message is among the user messages at the start of the current exchange.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.ResponseFormat
member.summary: Provider-native output format for this turn, including all tool-call iterations. Not inherited by later turns or subagents. Ordinary steering inherits the active format; specifying responseFormat with mode: immediate is an error, even while idle. Returned assistant content remains text; the runtime does not parse or validate it. Unsupported models or schemas produce provider errors.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.Source
member.summary: Optional provenance tag copied to the resulting user.message event. Must be `user`, `system`, `command-<command-id>` for command-originated messages, `schedule-<numeric-id>` for scheduled prompts, `agent-<agent-id>` for prompts sent by another agent, or `automation-<automation-id>` for turns a host sends on behalf of an automation the user configured. An automation turn defines the session's task like a user message but carries no human authority.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.Traceparent
member.summary: W3C Trace Context traceparent header for distributed tracing of this agent turn.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.Tracestate
member.summary: W3C Trace Context tracestate header for distributed tracing.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SendRequest.Wait
member.summary: If true, await completion of the agentic loop for this message before returning. Defaults to false (fire-and-forget). When true, the result still contains the same `messageId`; the caller can rely on the agent having processed the message before the call resolves. Transport-dependent tail semantics: on a LOCAL (in-process) session the wait additionally blocks until the completed turn's event tail has been dispatched to this session's in-process subscribers, so a subsequent read of subscriber state already reflects the turn; on a REMOTE session the wait resolves once the loop completes and mirrored delivery follows over the wire. Callers that need the stronger local guarantee on remote sessions should await the event stream explicitly.

member.summary: Whether the session ended up with a populated `copilotUser` for the installed credentials. `true` when the supplied credential already carried `copilotUser` or it was successfully re-resolved server-side. `false` when the credential is installed without `copilotUser` — either re-resolution failed, or the variant cannot be re-resolved from the credential alone (only the raw-token variants `token`, `env`, and `gh-cli` can). member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionSetCredentialsParams
member.summary: New auth credentials to install on the session. Omit to leave credentials unchanged.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionSetCredentialsParams.Credentials
member.summary: The new auth credentials to install on the session. When omitted or `undefined`, the call is a no-op and the session's existing credentials are preserved. The runtime installs the supplied value immediately for outbound model/API requests. When the credential carries a raw token (`token`, `env`, or `gh-cli`) but no `copilotUser`, the runtime additionally re-resolves `copilotUser` server-side (best-effort, asynchronously, after the synchronous install) so plan/quota/billing metadata regains fidelity; on resolution failure the verbatim credential remains installed. It does NOT otherwise validate the credential. Several variants carry secret material; treat this method's params as containing secrets at rest and in transit.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.AuthLoginStep
member.summary: One step in an interactive login flow. The consumer acts on the step and calls advance to proceed. Browser-open is encoded as two distinct steps by design: `open-url` is CONSUMER-driven (the provider surfaces the authorize URL and the consumer opens it — github.com/GHEC web), while `needs-interaction` is PROVIDER-driven (the provider opens the browser or broker UI itself and does not surface a URL — Entra). A device-code flow surfaces its one-time code as `device-code`; the consumer shows the code, may open the verification URI, and calls advance, which resolves once the user has authorized the device.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CurrentModel.FusionTier
member.summary: Copilot Fusion tier that the committed autoTier serves, resolved from the session's Auto tier metadata. An open string: known values include `standard`, `high`, and `max`; other provider-defined values may appear. Omitted when autoTier is unset, is not a Fusion tier, or Auto metadata has not been discovered (for example after cold resume, before session.model.list). This snapshot reports only the committed Fusion tier; resolve pendingAutoTier and activatingAutoTier against auto.tiers[].fusionTier from session.model.list.

member.summary: Explicit response to a model-switch compaction preflight. Omit to request a confirmation projection when compaction is necessary.

member.summary: Explicit context tier for the selected model. `"default"` / `"long_context"` apply the requested tier; omit this field to use normal model behavior with no explicit tier.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ModelSwitchToRequest.DeferIfModelChangeQueued
member.summary: When true, defer this switch (enqueue it) if another model change is already queued, even when no turn is active — so it drains last (FIFO) and wins over the already-queued change. Intended for genuine user-initiated model selections; internal restore/reapply switches omit it and apply immediately when no turn is active. When no other model change is queued this has no effect (a switch still applies immediately unless a turn is active).

member.summary: Model id to switch to, as returned by `list`. Include providerId to select an exact catalog entry when providers share the id. Without providerId, a bare id retains incumbent selection behavior; a registry-qualified id (`provider/id`, e.g. `acme/claude-sonnet`) targets a BYOK model.

"none" disables reasoning. Pass null to clear any session effort override and fall back to the model's default. When omitted, the session's current effort is kept.

member.summary: When true, evaluate context-window compaction policy before applying the switch, including effort-only and unchanged selections while idle. An effort-only change applies immediately without compaction when a turn is active, including when the turn starts during preflight; an explicit `compactionDecision: "cancel"` still cancels the change. member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ModelSetAllowedModelsRequest
member.summary: Host-supplied exact model selection IDs to allow for this running session. CAPI IDs are intersected with repository `.github/allowed_models.txt` policy; provider-qualified IDs remain exempt from repository-only policy but are restricted by this host list. Omit or pass null to clear the host restriction; an explicit empty or disjoint list is rejected. Validation and pre-selection fallback failures preserve the previous restriction. Failures after a fallback selection commits retain the new restriction and selected model; callers should inspect current session state after such an error.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ModelGetReasoningSummariesResult.ClearRedundantSetting
member.summary: Whether the supplied `persistedShowReasoning` setting only restates the model default. This reports a redundancy, not a standing instruction to delete the setting: it stays true for as long as the setting and the model default agree, including for a user who later chose that value deliberately. It exists for a one-time migration of a legacy setting written before the model default made it redundant, so a host that acts on it owns the cleanup and must gate it behind its own persisted `done` marker, delete only a setting whose value still matches the one it read, and never repeat the deletion on a later launch. Under an off-by-default reasoning-summaries experiment an explicit `showReasoning: true` opt-in also reads as redundant on a summary-producing model, so an ungated host would keep deleting that opt-in and hide summaries again on every launch.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ModelGetReasoningSummariesResult.ExperimentSettled
member.summary: Whether the session's reasoning-summaries experiment assignment has settled. False means this read does not wait for a pending assignment and reports the experiment-derived fields conservatively: `showHiddenHint` is false and `visibility` falls back to `persistedShowReasoning`, or is omitted when none was supplied. A host that wants the assigned answer re-reads until this is true.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ModelGetReasoningSummariesResult.ModelDefaultShowsSummaries
member.summary: Whether the selected model shows reasoning summaries by default.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ModelGetReasoningSummariesResult.Ready
member.summary: False until the session has a model catalog and a selected model. This read never resolves the catalog itself, and the runtime emits no readiness notification, so repeating this call alone leaves `ready` false indefinitely on a session that has neither listed models nor run a turn. `session.model.list` is the prerequisite and the signal: it resolves and caches the catalog for the session, so a successful return means the next read is ready. The exception is a session that resolves models without a Copilot catalog, that is a BYOK registry or an alternate provider: `session.model.list` returns an empty list without caching a catalog, so `ready` stays false and this policy is unavailable there. While false, every model-policy field is false and `visibility` is omitted; `experimentSettled` is independent of readiness and still reports the assignment state.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ModelGetReasoningSummariesResult.SessionShowsSummaries
member.summary: Whether turns on this session produce reasoning summaries, honouring an explicit session reasoning-summary override.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ModelGetReasoningSummariesResult.ShowHiddenHint
member.summary: Whether to show the hint that reasoning summaries are hidden. Always false while `experimentSettled` is false.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ModelGetReasoningSummariesResult.ShowReasoningHeaders
member.summary: Whether the selected model emits reasoning headers.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ModelGetReasoningSummariesResult.Visibility
member.summary: Default reasoning visibility, and only meaningful once `ready` is true: false when the session produces no summaries, else the persisted setting, else the experiment's default. While `ready` is true it is omitted only when all three are unavailable, that is when the session produces summaries, no `persistedShowReasoning` was supplied, and `experimentSettled` is false. While `ready` is false there is no model policy to report and this field is always omitted, so an absent value alone does not imply a pending experiment.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.WorkspaceDiffResult.UnavailableReason
member.summary: Why the session diff could not be produced, when applicable. Set only when `session` mode was requested and `isFallback` is true, so a client can tell the permanent `file-change-tracking-disabled` apart from the transient `session-busy`, which the same request answers once the session settles. Never set for `unstaged` or `branch` mode, and never `unsupported-remote-session`: a remote session's captures live on its own host, so a `session`-mode diff is rejected for one rather than answered with a controller-side fallback.

member.summary: Include the full before/after text used to compute each session diff. Defaults to false; true is accepted only for session mode. Existing capture/read limits still apply, and binary or unavailable contents are not returned. This can substantially increase response size.

member.summary: Output a detached shell task wrote after the request cursor, with the cursor for the next read.

member.summary: Opaque cursor to pass to the next read of this task. Always present, even when no output was returned.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TasksReadOutputResult.Exit
member.summary: Present once the shell has finished and this read reaches the end of its output. Later reads with the returned cursor return no new text and the same exit details.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TasksReadOutputResult.Text
member.summary: Output after the request cursor, decoded as UTF-8 and redacted. At most 64 KiB per read, so a large backlog takes several reads; the text never splits a character, and text that stops before the end of the output ends at a line break when it contains one. Empty when no new output is available. Detached shells write stdout and stderr to one output, so the text does not separate them.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TasksReadOutputRequest
member.summary: Detached shell task to read output from, with an optional cursor and long-poll wait. waitMs defaults to zero (maximum 30000).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TasksReadOutputRequest.Cursor
member.summary: Opaque cursor returned by an earlier read of the same task. Omit to read from the beginning of the shell's output. If the output no longer reaches the cursor, for example because its log was removed, the request fails; read again without a cursor.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TasksReadOutputRequest.Id
member.summary: Identifier of a detached shell task, as returned by tasks.list.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TasksReadOutputRequest.SessionId
member.summary: Target session identifier.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TasksReadOutputRequest.Wait
member.summary: Milliseconds to wait for new output, or for the shell to finish, when the cursor is already at the end of the available output. 0 (default) returns immediately. Capped at 30000ms.

member.summary: OAuth authorization URL the caller should open, or empty when cached tokens already authenticated the server.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginResult.AuthorizationId
member.summary: Opaque authorization identifier returned only for a host-managed redirect URI. The runtime also sends it as the OAuth state value, so the callback endpoint can read state and pass it with the full callback URL to session.mcp.oauth.complete.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginResult.AuthorizationUrl
member.summary: URL the caller should open in a browser to complete OAuth. Omitted when cached tokens were still valid and no browser interaction was needed — the server is already reconnected in that case. For the default loopback flow, the runtime starts its listener before returning. With redirectUri, the host receives the callback and completes it through session.mcp.oauth.complete. The runtime continues the flow in the background and signals completion via session.mcp_server_status_changed.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginResult.LoginId
member.summary: Runtime-issued owned flow identity; never a server name or installation operation ID.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginResult.Status
member.summary: Explicit outcome for owned sign-in. Manual callers retain their legacy response shape.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginRequest.CallbackSuccessMessage
member.summary: Optional override for the body text shown on the OAuth loopback callback success page. When omitted, the runtime applies a neutral fallback; callers driving interactive auth should pass surface-specific copy telling the user where to return.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginRequest.ClientId
member.summary: Optional OAuth client ID override for this login. When set, the runtime uses this pre-registered static client instead of dynamic client registration.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginRequest.ClientName
member.summary: Optional override for the OAuth client display name shown on the consent screen. Applies to newly registered dynamic clients only — existing registrations keep the name they were created with. When omitted, the runtime applies a neutral fallback; callers driving interactive auth should pass their own surface-specific label so the consent screen matches the product the user sees.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginRequest.ClientSecret
member.summary: Optional OAuth client secret override for this login. The runtime treats this as an ephemeral host-owned secret, uses it for this authentication attempt and does not persist it.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginRequest.ExpectedInstallationId
member.summary: Exact owned receipt identity. Owned login never uses an implicit helper session.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginRequest.ForceReauth
member.summary: When true, clears any cached OAuth token for the server and runs a full new authorization. Use when the user explicitly wants to switch accounts or believes their session is stuck.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginRequest.GrantType
member.summary: Optional OAuth grant type override for this login. Defaults to the server configuration, or authorization_code when no grant type is specified.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginRequest.LoginId
member.summary: Required for owned login. Consumes the exact prepareLogin handle once. Set forceReauth and display options during preparation, not consumption.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginRequest.PublicClient
member.summary: Optional override indicating whether the static OAuth client is public. When false, the runtime treats it as confidential and uses the per-login clientSecret if provided, otherwise retrieving the client secret from the MCP OAuth secret store.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.McpOauthLoginRequest.RedirectUri
member.summary: Optional externally visible HTTPS redirect URI for a host-managed callback endpoint. When supplied, the runtime still owns discovery, PKCE, token exchange, persistence, and reconnect, but does not bind a loopback listener or terminate HTTPS. The URI must not contain query parameters or a fragment and must be registered for the selected CIMD, DCR, or static OAuth client.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ProtocolImageGenerationOptions
member.summary: Opt into native CAPI image generation.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ProtocolImageGenerationOptions.Enabled
member.summary: Disabled by default for SDK sessions. CAPI model access and permissions still apply.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ProtocolImageGenerationOptions.SaveToDisk
member.summary: Experimental. Save each generated or edited image under the session-state directory's `images` folder and add a `saved_to: <path>` line per image to the tool result the model sees. Defaults to true; set false to opt out. Subagents follow their parent's value unless they set their own. A failed save still returns the image, without `saved_to`. Sessions without a local session-state directory, such as those using a session filesystem provider, never save. Re-supply after a cold resume. Does not enable image generation. This option may change or be removed in a future release.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ProtocolImageGenerationOptions.Watermark
member.summary: Experimental. Request a visible "Made with AI" label on generated and edited images. This option may change or be removed in a future release. Overrides the user's imageGenerationWatermark preference for this session; otherwise that preference applies, defaulting to false. Re-supply after a cold resume. Does not enable image generation or enforce enterprise policy.

member.summary: Installation timestamp (ISO-8601).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionInstalledPlugin.InstalledFrom
member.summary: Absolute path of the marketplace directory a live plugin was resolved from. Present only on live, never-persisted records — those synthesized at session start for a directory/local marketplace, whose cache_path points at the real plugin directory on disk rather than a copy under the installed-plugins cache. Its presence is what marks a record as live, and no record carrying it is ever written to the persisted installedPlugins key.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionInstalledPlugin.InstalledSource
member.summary: Installation-time marketplace or direct source, independent of mutable marketplace aliases. Local paths are absolute. Absent for older installs; reinstall to record provenance.

member.summary: Marketplace the plugin came from (empty string for direct repo installs).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionInstalledPlugin.Name
member.summary: Plugin name.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionInstalledPlugin.Source
member.summary: Source descriptor for direct repo installs (when marketplace is empty).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionInstalledPlugin.SourceSha
member.summary: Per-plugin source fingerprint (a SHA-256 hash of the plugin's catalog source spec plus its resolved source subtree — NOT a Git commit SHA) captured at marketplace install/update time. Auto-update compares it against the freshly recomputed fingerprint to detect a content change that does not bump the version. Absent for pre-existing installs and for direct (non-marketplace) installs.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UIRegisterDirectAutoModeSwitchHandlerResult
member.summary: Registers an in-process Auto-switch responder and suppresses server-bridge dispatch to avoid competing responders for the same requestId. When requested, also enrolls the responder for active-request Auto recovery and acknowledges support. Attach the actual listener separately through standard event subscriptions before starting a turn, and release the handle when the responder is removed.

member.summary: Positive acknowledgment of recovery-aware enrollment. Absence on an older runtime means recovery is unsupported.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UIRegisterDirectAutoModeSwitchHandlerResult.Handle
member.summary: Opaque handle representing the registration. Pass this same handle to `unregisterDirectAutoModeSwitchHandler` when the in-process handler is no longer active. Multiple registrations are reference-counted; the server bridge will only dispatch auto-mode-switch requests when no handles are active.

member.summary: RPC data type for SessionUiRegisterDirectAutoModeSwitchHandler operations.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionUiRegisterDirectAutoModeSwitchHandlerRequest.AutoModeRecovery
member.summary: Opt into active-request Auto recovery before starting a turn. Attach the handler separately, show the failure reason, and return the user's choice for the originating live session. Require a positive acknowledgment in the registration result. Dismiss offers on auto_mode_recovery_consent.completed and on session resume or disconnect. Omitted or false preserves legacy rate-limit switching.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.AuthenticatedAuthorityGrant
member.summary: Bounded, lifecycle-fenced host authority rendered to the Assisted Permissions judge. Source-specific meaning and scope remain opaque data interpreted by the judge. The source must match the enclosing update source. At most 8 statements of up to 1,024 characters each (4,096 total), and at most 8 user messages of 16,384 characters in total; a grant needs at least one statement or user message. Scope follows the assisted-approval context JSON bounds. A session holds at most 8 active sources and 32 KiB of rendered grants, not counting user messages, and at most one active source may quote user messages.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.AuthenticatedAuthorityGrant.ExpiresAt
member.summary: RFC 3339 expiry timestamp.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.AuthenticatedAuthorityGrant.GrantId
member.summary: Stable host-issued identifier for this authority.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.AuthenticatedAuthorityGrant.Scope
member.summary: Structured scope facts constraining the authority statements. Must be an empty object when `statements` is empty.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.AuthenticatedAuthorityGrant.Source
member.summary: Stable identifier for the trusted authority source; must match the update source.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.AuthenticatedAuthorityGrant.Statements
member.summary: Bounded human-readable authority statements rendered to the judge. May be an empty array, never null, only when `userMessages` is not empty; a grant without statements adds no grant record to the judge's system prompt, so its `scope` must then be an empty object.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.AuthenticatedAuthorityGrant.UserMessages
member.summary: The user's own messages in another session, verbatim and oldest first, that the host authenticates as the user's, such as what the user wrote to the session that delegated work to this one. The judge transcript shows each as one of the user's own messages, written in another session, before this session's own user messages. Never include text an agent, tool, or file wrote. Only one active source may quote user messages, because quotes from different sources have no order, and only while the session has no human messages of its own, which could be older or newer than the quotes; human messages the session receives later render after the quotes. Omit when the grant quotes no user messages.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.AuthenticatedAuthorityUpdate
member.summary: Replaces or revokes one source's revocable session-scoped authority from the owning host. A non-null grant replaces only the named source; null revokes only the named source. The revision always advances the session-global fence.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.AuthenticatedAuthorityUpdate.Grant
member.summary: Replacement authority, or null to revoke the named source.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.AuthenticatedAuthorityUpdate.Revision
member.summary: Monotonically increasing host-issued revision, from 1 to 2^53 - 1 so every SDK represents it exactly.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.AuthenticatedAuthorityUpdate.Source
member.summary: Stable source whose independent authority slot is being updated.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.PermissionPathsConfig.AdditionalDirectories
member.summary: Additional directories to allow tool access to (in addition to the session's working directory). Conventional `.github/skills/` and `.github/agents/` definitions under them also join the session catalogs when their subsystem gates are enabled, so supplying a directory is a trust decision for configuration stored there. When `unrestricted` is true, these are still pre-populated on the UnrestrictedPathManager so they remain visible via getDirectories() (e.g. for @-mention completion).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.PermissionsConfigureParams.AssistedApprovalContext
member.summary: SDK-host advisory JSON for future Assisted Permissions judge requests. The value replaces only its named source; null clears that source. Omit to leave all sources unchanged. The runtime applies strict structural and size limits, renders the source in a runtime-controlled advisory frame, and never treats the value as instructions or authorization. Session-scoped only; hosts must reapply after resume.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.PermissionsConfigureParams.AssistedApprovalInstructions
member.summary: User-authored instructions appended verbatim to the assisted-approval judge's system prompt. Applies to subsequent judge requests in this local session without changing permission mode, pre-judge gates, or the coding agent's prompt. Omit to leave unchanged; an empty or whitespace-only string clears the instructions. Hosts must reapply their configuration after resuming a session. Remote sessions are not supported.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.PermissionsConfigureParams.AuthenticatedAuthority
member.summary: Optional owner-authenticated per-source update to lifecycle-fenced session authority. Active grants from all sources are rendered together, in source order, to the Assisted Permissions judge, which alone interprets their statements and scope. Only the owning non-extension session connection, bound to the current session generation, may replace or revoke authority. Omit to leave unchanged. Hard runtime controls, mandatory policy, and later human restrictions still take precedence. Session-scoped only; hosts must reapply after resume.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.PermissionsConfigureParams.HostPolicyPermissionHandler
member.summary: Declares whether this connection's registered permission handler applies non-human host policy to the tools and canvases this connection registered. When true, unattended Assisted Autopilot sends permission requests for those tools, and `open_canvas` and `invoke_canvas_action` requests whose target canvas this connection registered, to the handler before runtime Assisted Approval or unattended fallback can settle them. All other requests, including shell commands, file access, URLs, and tools or canvases registered by other connections or extensions, keep runtime settlement. Managed policy and other runtime enforcement still take precedence. Only the session's owning non-extension connection may set this field. The declaration ends when that connection detaches or the session is resumed, so hosts must reapply it after resume. Omit to leave unchanged; false clears it. Without a declaration, registered handlers are not consulted during unattended Assisted Autopilot. Remote sessions are not supported.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.MetadataRecordContextChangeResult
member.summary: Notify the session that its working directory context has changed. Emits a `session.context_changed` event so consumers (telemetry, OTel tracker, ACP, the timeline UI) can react. Use this when the host has detected a cwd/branch/repo change outside the session's normal lifecycle (e.g., after a shell command in interactive mode). For a local session, a report whose `cwd` diverges from the session's current working directory is ignored (the call still succeeds but records nothing and emits no event); move a local session's working directory via `metadata.setWorkingDirectory` instead.

member.summary: Target session identifier.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.MetadataSetWorkingDirectoryResult
member.summary: Update the session's working directory. Used by the host when the user explicitly changes cwd (e.g., the `/cd` slash command). The host is responsible for any related side-effects (file index, etc.); it does NOT change the process working directory (a session's cwd is per-session, not process-global). For local sessions the runtime validates the target first (an absolute path that exists on disk) and re-bases the permission primary directory; a rejected validation fails the call before anything is mutated, persisted, or emitted. Location-scoped permission rules are then re-keyed to the new directory (best-effort). Remote sessions only record the path.

Applies when the model that summarizes supports it; otherwise the request keeps its usual effort. Takes precedence over any runtime experiment that adjusts compaction reasoning effort. member.summary: Cursor, batch size, and optional long-poll/filter parameters for reading session events.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequest.AgentIds
member.summary: Optional non-empty list of subagent identifiers. When provided, only events owned by one of these agents are returned; ownership recognizes the event envelope's agentId plus legacy data.agentId and data.parentToolCallId markers. This filter takes precedence over agentScope.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequest.AgentScope
member.summary: Agent-scope filter: 'primary' returns only main-agent events plus events whose type starts with 'subagent.' (matching the typed-subscription default behavior); 'all' returns events from all agents (matching wildcard-subscription behavior). Default is 'all' to preserve wildcard semantics for catch-up callers.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequest.Cursor
member.summary: Opaque cursor returned by a previous read in the same view. Omit on the first call to start from the beginning of the selected view.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequest.Direction
member.summary: Direction to page through the session's persisted event history. 'forward' (default) pages from the cursor toward newer events (or from the start of history when no cursor is given). 'backward' enables tail-first reads: with no cursor it returns the NEWEST `max` events, and the returned cursor pages toward OLDER events on subsequent backward reads. Events within a returned batch are always in chronological (oldest-to-newest) order, even for a backward read. Backward reads cover PERSISTED history only; ephemeral events are never returned by a backward read. `direction` selects the INITIAL read only: the returned cursor is self-describing, so a continuation read pages in the cursor's own direction regardless of the `direction` passed alongside it — a forward cursor always pages forward and a backward cursor always pages backward. Pass the direction that matches the cursor to avoid confusion.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequest.IncludeEphemeral
member.summary: When false, skip ephemeral events entirely and return only durable (persisted) events. History-backfill callers that discard ephemerals anyway should set this so the read is bounded by the durable log length instead of racing the ephemeral ring on a busy session. Defaults to true (ephemerals are interleaved with durable events in creation order). Ignored by backward reads, which always cover persisted history only.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequest.Max
member.summary: Maximum number of events to return in this batch (1–1000, default 200).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequest.Types
member.summary: Either '*' to receive all event types, or a non-empty list of event types to receive.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequest.View
member.summary: Event stream to read. 'history' (default) returns original events and lazily follows predecessor journals, excluding checkpoint copies. 'replay' reads only the active replay head, including checkpoint state, without opening predecessor journals. Use replay for current state and fast transcript previews; use history to reconstruct the original visible transcript. Cursors must remain within the view that produced them.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequest.Wait
member.summary: Milliseconds to wait for new events when the cursor is at the tail of history. 0 (default) returns immediately even if no events are available. Capped at 30000ms. Ephemeral events that arrive during the wait are delivered in this batch but are NOT replayable on a subsequent read (use a non-zero waitMs in your next call to capture future ephemerals as they happen). This applies to forward reads only: a backward read always returns immediately and ignores `waitMs`, because backward paging covers persisted history only while new events append at the tail (the opposite end from a backward page), so no blocking or ephemeral delivery can occur.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequestWithSession.AgentScope

'backward' enables tail-first reads: with no cursor it returns the NEWEST `max` events, and the returned cursor pages toward OLDER events on subsequent backward reads. Events within a returned batch are always in chronological (oldest-to-newest) order, even for a backward read. Backward reads cover PERSISTED history only; ephemeral events are never returned by a backward read. `direction` selects the INITIAL read only: the returned cursor is self-describing, so a continuation read pages in the cursor's own direction regardless of the `direction` passed alongside it — a forward cursor always pages forward and a backward cursor always pages backward. Pass the direction that matches the cursor to avoid confusion.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequestWithSession.IncludeEphemeral
member.summary: When false, skip ephemeral events entirely and return only durable (persisted) events. History-backfill callers that discard ephemerals anyway should set this so the read is bounded by the durable log length instead of racing the ephemeral ring on a busy session. Defaults to true (ephemerals are interleaved with durable events in creation order). Ignored by backward reads, which always cover persisted history only.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequestWithSession.Max
member.summary: Maximum number of events to return in this batch (1–1000, default 200).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequestWithSession.SessionId
member.summary: Target session identifier.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequestWithSession.Types
member.summary: Either '*' to receive all event types, or a non-empty list of event types to receive.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequestWithSession.View
member.summary: Event stream to read. 'history' (default) returns original events and lazily follows predecessor journals, excluding checkpoint copies. 'replay' reads only the active replay head, including checkpoint state, without opening predecessor journals. Use replay for current state and fast transcript previews; use history to reconstruct the original visible transcript. Cursors must remain within the view that produced them.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogReadRequestWithSession.Wait
member.summary: Milliseconds to wait for new events when the cursor is at the tail of history. 0 (default) returns immediately even if no events are available. Capped at 30000ms. Ephemeral events that arrive during the wait are delivered in this batch but are NOT replayable on a subsequent read (use a non-zero waitMs in your next call to capture future ephemerals as they happen). This applies to forward reads only: a backward read always returns immediately and ignores `waitMs`, because backward paging covers persisted history only while new events append at the tail (the opposite end from a backward page), so no blocking or ephemeral delivery can occur.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogTailResult
member.summary: Snapshot of the current tail cursor without returning any events. Use this when a consumer wants to subscribe to live events going forward without first paginating through the entire persisted history (which would happen if `read` were called without a cursor on a long-lived session).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogTailResult.Cursor
member.summary: Opaque cursor pointing at the current tail of the session's persisted-events history. Pass back to `read` to receive only events that arrive AFTER this snapshot. When the session has no events, this returns the same sentinel as an unset cursor (i.e. equivalent to omitting the cursor on a first read).

member.summary: Opaque handle representing an event-type interest registration.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.RegisterEventInterestResult.Handle
member.summary: Opaque handle for this registration. Pass to releaseInterest to release. Each call to registerInterest produces a fresh handle, even when the same eventType is registered multiple times.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.RegisterEventInterestParams
member.summary: Event type to register consumer interest for, used by runtime gating logic.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.RegisterEventInterestParams.EventType
member.summary: The event type the consumer wants the runtime to treat as 'observed' for behavior-switching gating. Some runtime code paths inspect whether any consumer is interested in a specific event type and choose a different implementation accordingly (e.g. `mcp.oauth_required`: when interest is registered the runtime delegates interactive OAuth token acquisition to the consumer via `mcp.oauth_required` events; when no interest is registered the runtime still attempts non-interactive reconnect from cached or refreshable tokens, and only marks the server `needs-auth` if usable credentials are unavailable — it does not open a browser or start interactive OAuth without a consumer). SDK clients that long-poll events do NOT automatically appear as listeners to these gating checks — they must explicitly call `registerInterest` for each event type they want the runtime to count as having a consumer. Multiple registrations for the same event type from the same or different consumers are tracked independently and must each be released. See: `mcp.oauth_required`, `sampling.requested`, `auto_mode_switch.requested`, `session_limits_exhausted.requested`, `user_input.requested`, `elicitation.requested`, `command.queued`, `exit_plan_mode.requested`.

member.summary: Stable identity of the agent trajectory that issued this request. Present when the request originates from an agent turn; absent for requests outside any agent context. This is the same identity used by lifecycle and bridged session events and remains constant across turns and retries.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.LlmInferenceHttpRequestStartRequest.AgentInvocationId
member.summary: Identity of the agent invocation (one agentic loop) that issued this request. It remains fixed across physical retries within the invocation and is distinct from the stable trajectory `agentId`. A caller-supplied invocation id always takes precedence (this covers auxiliary calls that have no model call id). Otherwise, first-party CAPI requests fall back to the runtime's agent task id — the same value the runtime emits as the `X-Agent-Task-Id` header — while custom-provider requests fall back to the model call id.

Open string for forward-compatibility; known values include `conversation-agent`, `conversation-subagent`, `conversation-sampling`, `conversation-background`, `conversation-compaction`, and `conversation-user`. Absent when the runtime did not classify the request. Comes from the runtime's per-request agent context independently of transport; on the CAPI transport the runtime derives the upstream `X-Interaction-Type` header from this same context.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.LlmInferenceHttpRequestStartRequest.SessionId
member.summary: Id of the runtime session that triggered this request, when one is in scope. Absent for requests issued outside any session (e.g. startup model-catalog or capability resolution). This is a payload field — not a dispatch key — because the client-global API is registered process-wide rather than per session.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.LlmInferenceHttpRequestStartRequest.Transport
member.summary: Transport the runtime would otherwise use for this request. `http` (the default when absent) covers plain HTTP and SSE responses; `websocket` indicates a full-duplex message channel where each body chunk maps to one WebSocket message and the `binary` flag distinguishes text from binary frames. The SDK consumer uses this to decide whether to service the request with an HTTP client or a WebSocket client. It is the one piece of request metadata the consumer cannot reliably infer from the URL or headers alone.

member.summary: Identity of the agent invocation (one agentic loop) this body chunk belongs to, matching the `agentInvocationId` semantics on httpRequestStart. Carried per chunk so a persistent transport can attribute successive turns correctly: when a WebSocket connection is reused across turns, the httpRequestStart identity reflects only the turn that opened the connection, so each later turn stamps its own invocation id here. member.summary: A wire feature a caller can require of the catalog surface, negotiated per request. A grant means the runtime understands the feature's contract, not that the deployment has enabled the operation; typed unavailable results report availability separately.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.#ctor(System.String)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the struct.
member.param: The value to associate with this .

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.Value
member.summary: Gets the value associated with this .

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.McpServerCard
member.summary: Understands the current `application/mcp-server-card+json` media type.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.LegacyMcpServerCard
member.summary: Understands the legacy `application/mcp-server+json` media type.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.AiSkillDiscovery
member.summary: Understands `application/ai-skill` candidates as discovery-only and typed non-installable.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.AgentPluginDiscovery
member.summary: Understands opt-in `application/vnd.github.copilot-plugin` candidates and their typed identity, version, source, and compatibility fields.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.AgentPluginFormats
member.summary: Extends agent-plugin-discovery to Claude plugin (`application/vnd.anthropic.claude-plugin+json`) and portable Agent Plugin (`application/agent-plugin+json`) candidates, each reporting its format as its media type. Requires agent-plugin-discovery; without it, plugin searches return only Copilot plugins.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.McpInstallPlanning
member.summary: Understands side-effect-free MCP install-plan requests, results, and plan handles; `planning-unavailable` separately reports that planning is not enabled.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.MultipleTransportChoice
member.summary: Understands plans that enumerate every eligible transport rather than a single preferred one.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.CatalogSearchPagination
member.summary: Understands explicit numbered navigation and authority-reported pagination metadata with opaque tokens. Advertised and granted only when requested.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.TrustSnapshot
member.summary: Understands versioned candidate trust snapshots. Protocol-3 callers must require this capability before the runtime adds the optional snapshot field.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.CatalogSelection
member.summary: Understands exact candidate selection through model-safe opaque references and host-only candidate-handle hand-off.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.CatalogSearchCredentialRequired
member.summary: Requires an eligible credential for the selected GitHub.com account before search egress and prohibits client-side anonymous retry, including after HTTP 401 or 403. The credential is scoped to the fixed catalog authority without redirect forwarding. Neither a grant nor successful response proves that the authority accepted the identity or selected a particular backend. Preserve this requirement on every page and retry; callers omitting it retain optional authentication.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.CatalogSearchSessionBound
member.summary: Captures the exact existing native session, account, host and connection for authenticated catalogue search, selection and planning. Requires catalog-search-credential-required; does not grant installation or create a session.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.CatalogRecommend
member.summary: Understands initial-page official-product recommendations for a full task and product with fixed pageSize 10. Requires session-bound, credential-required catalogue support. No anonymous retry, broad-search fallback or continuation. Authentication uses the selected GitHub.com user credential; successful capability negotiation does not establish service acceptance.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.McpConfirmedRemoteInstallation
member.summary: Understands effect-free preparation, exact human-confirmed apply and owned removal for fully resolved personal remote MCP choices without supplied inputs or configured secrets. Advertised only when the real producer and lower owned admission are linked; requires original connection and bound session authority for new work.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.McpConfiguredRemoteInstallation
member.summary: Extends mcp-confirmed-remote-installation to declared non-secret header and URL values and receipt-owned header secrets for personal remote MCP choices. Requires mcp-confirmed-remote-installation and bound session authority. Secret values are written only to the reviewed backend after confirmation and are never returned; package and stdio choices remain unsupported. Advertised only when owned secret effects and owned secret activation are linked.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.SkillConfirmedInstallation
member.summary: Understands verified Agent Finder Skill install, uninstall, recovery and installation-scoped enablement APIs. Advertised only by runtimes with the Skill installation engine linked; acquisition may still be refused as feature-disabled per selected session.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.AgentPluginConfirmedInstallation
member.summary: Understands `installability`, the reviewable `installPlan` and the optional materialisation `handle` on Agent Plugin candidates, and the verified Agent Plugin installation APIs plugins.planInstall and plugins.applyInstall, and Agent Plugin plans from catalog.planInstallFromReference. Requires agent-plugin-discovery; without it, plugin candidates are unchanged. Advertised only by runtimes with the plugin installer linked; acquisition may still be refused as feature-disabled per selected session.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.CatalogReferenceInstallation
member.summary: Understands catalog.planInstallFromReference, which plans installing whatever resource an Agent Finder materialisation reference pins. It plans only kinds whose installation capability the caller also requires: skill-confirmed-installation for Skills, agent-plugin-confirmed-installation for Agent Plugins. Advertised only by runtimes with the Skill installation engine linked.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.CatalogFeeds
member.summary: Understands catalog.getSavedFeed and catalog.getGeneratedFeed, which retrieve a saved or generated feed with entries projected exactly like catalog.search candidates. Requires catalog-search-credential-required; add catalog-search-session-bound to bind the retrieval to a selected session.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.CatalogCapability.CatalogSearchCategories
member.summary: Understands the optional `categories` filter on catalog.search, which the runtime forwards to the catalog authority. Required to send the filter, so an older runtime refuses the request instead of silently returning unfiltered results.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventsCursorStatus
member.summary: Cursor status: 'ok' means the read succeeded against the requested history; 'expired' means the requested continuation is unavailable. Recovery is endpoint-specific: session.eventLog.read returns a boundary window of remaining active history that may overlap prior pages, while sessions.readPersistedEvents returns an empty terminal page and never switches journal generations. An expired persisted read is not successful completion; a complete persisted snapshot requires cursorStatus 'ok' and hasMore false.

member.summary: A conversation-and-files rewind was requested for a session that did not enable capture; conversation-only rewinds never produce this.

member.summary: Remote-backed rewind routing is not supported; reachable in either mode.

member.summary: File restore failed and all applied file changes were rolled back; only conversation-and-files rewinds produce this.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HistoryRewindOutcome.RollbackIncomplete
member.summary: File restore failed and its rollback could not fully restore the pre-rewind state; only conversation-and-files rewinds produce this.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HistoryRewindOutcome.TruncationFailed
member.summary: Conversation truncation failed. In conversation-and-files mode any files that were restored are left in place because conversation history cannot be un-truncated; in conversation-only mode no files are restored. Consult restoredFiles for what, if anything, was applied.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HistoryRewindOutcome.CheckpointCleanupFailed
member.summary: The conversation was rewound (and, in conversation-and-files mode, captured files were restored), but persisted checkpoints could not be cleaned up; reachable in either mode.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HistoryRewindOutcome.SnapshotPruneFailed
member.summary: Files and conversation were rewound, but obsolete file snapshots could not be removed; only conversation-and-files rewinds produce this.

member.summary: Checks server responsiveness and returns protocol information.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerRpc.ConnectAsync(GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EntraAuthConfig,System.Nullable{System.Boolean},System.Nullable{System.Boolean},GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ConnectClientInfo,System.Collections.Generic.IList{GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.TaskKind},System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Performs the SDK server connection handshake and validates the optional connection token. Marked internal because this is JSON-RPC transport plumbing invoked automatically by an SDK client's own `connect()` wrapper, not a user-facing method. Stays internal as long as the SDK client owns the handshake; would only become public if the SDK ever exposed the raw schema surface to consumers without a connection wrapper.
member.param: Entra application used by this client's authentication flows. Required to enable built-in Microsoft Entra sign-in and token renewal; other authentication methods remain available.

Opt this connection in to host-owned Entra identity and token acquisition through entraToken.getToken. Requires entra.clientId and an explicit true acknowledgement in the response. SDKs set this internally when a callback is configured.

Opt this connection in to GitHub telemetry forwarding for its lifetime. When set, the runtime forwards this host's telemetry across all its sessions, its sessionless events, and explicitly process-wide events over the `gitHubTelemetry.event` notification. Connections intentionally sharing one server receive that server's events; independently embedded runtime hosts do not receive each other's host-owned events. Regular events are also written to the runtime's normal GitHub/CTS path (dual-write); host-only compatibility events are forward-only and intentionally skip that path. Intended for first-party hosts that re-emit the events into their own telemetry stores. Both unrestricted and restricted events are forwarded, each tagged with a `restricted` discriminator; a backstop drops restricted events when restricted telemetry is disabled — using the process-global gate for ordinary events and an explicit session-scoped decision for host-only events.
Identity of the integrating host. Optional; omit it to keep the default attribution.
Task kinds this connection can decode when observing session tasks. Omit to retain agent and shell compatibility.
Connection token; required when the server was started with COPILOT_CONNECTION_TOKEN.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Handshake result reporting the server's protocol version and package version on success.
