member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSandboxApi
member.summary: Provides server-scoped Sandbox APIs.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSandboxApi.ResolveFlooredConfigAsync(System.Object,System.Object,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Raises a user's sandbox settings to an administrator's managed sandbox floor and returns the result a session should actually run under. The floor can only tighten: an enterprise force-on is reflected even when the user's own `enabled` is false, and a user cannot lower a setting the floor raised. The result is normalized through the declared sandbox shape, so a key reorder or an undeclared passthrough key is not mistaken for a policy change by callers that diff two results. A host must call this rather than merge the two layers itself, because reimplementing the direction of the fold is what turns an administrator's floor into a suggestion.
member.param: The user's own `sandbox` settings slice. Omitted when the user has configured none, which still yields the managed floor rather than a disabled sandbox.
The effective managed `sandbox` slice acting as a floor. Omitted when no administrator policy applies, in which case the user's own settings stand unchanged.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: The user's sandbox settings raised to the managed floor.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSandboxApi.PreparePickerPolicyAsync(System.String,System.Object,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Builds the effective filesystem policy one `@`-file picker checks its suggestions against, so Git discovery and grant canonicalization run once for the picker's lifetime instead of on every debounced keystroke. Returns no policy when the sandbox is absent or disabled, which the paired filter reads as "keep every candidate". A host must pair this with `sandbox.filterPickerCandidates` rather than resolve a grant list itself, because the picker's grants are narrower than a file tool's — the same path a built-in tool may read can be one the picker must not offer.
member.param: The session's working directory. Git discovery and grant canonicalization are resolved against it.
The session's resolved `sandbox` slice. Omitted, or disabled, yields no policy and every candidate is kept.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: The prepared file-picker policy, or none when the sandbox is disabled.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSandboxApi.FilterPickerCandidatesAsync(System.Collections.Generic.IList{GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SandboxPickerCandidate},System.String,System.Object,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Checks a batch of `@`-file picker suggestions against a policy prepared by `sandbox.preparePickerPolicy` and returns one allow decision per candidate, positionally aligned with the request. Batched deliberately: each check canonicalizes a path component-by-component through the real filesystem, so one call amortizes that over a single hop rather than dozens while the user types. A directory the policy does not itself allow can still be kept as a waypoint to an allowed subtree. An absent policy keeps every candidate.
member.param: The candidates to check, in the order the answers are returned.
The session's working directory, matching the one the policy was prepared from.
The policy returned by `sandbox.preparePickerPolicy`. Omitted keeps every candidate.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Per-candidate allow decisions, positionally aligned with the request.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSandboxApi.ResolveForOptionalAsync(System.String,System.Object,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: The sandbox a single named feature actually launches under, which is not the same as the session's sandbox. A feature is routed out of the sandbox by its own flag — `sandboxMcpServers`, `sandboxLspServers` — so an enabled session can still start one server confined and another free. Returns a disabled sandbox rather than an error when the host has no sandbox slice at all, so an absent config and an opted-out feature read alike at the launch site. A host must ask per feature rather than reuse the session config, because reading only `enabled` confines a server the user opted out of, or reports as sandboxed one that is not.
member.param: The routing flag naming the feature being launched, such as `sandboxMcpServers` or `sandboxLspServers`.
The session's resolved `sandbox` slice. Omitted when the host has none, which yields a disabled sandbox rather than an error.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: The sandbox a named feature actually launches under.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSandboxApi.CheckPlatformSupportAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Reports whether this machine can run an OS-level command sandbox at all. A host must ask before it offers sandboxing, because the answer is a property of the machine rather than of any setting: on Linux it depends on bubblewrap being installed, and on Windows on the OS build supporting BaseContainer. Probing it requires spawning a process the first time, so the answer is cached for the life of the runtime. A host that assumes support and enables the sandbox anyway produces a session in which every shell command fails.
member.param: The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: True when an OS-level sandbox can run on this host.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSandboxApi.CheckWindowsHostLoopbackSupportAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Reports whether this Windows host's BaseContainer implementation can reach the host's loopback interface directly, which is what a local-network policy needs to avoid routing through the egress proxy. Like `sandbox.checkPlatformSupport`, the answer is a property of the machine's OS build rather than of any setting, and resolving it the first time spawns a platform probe. A host that offers the direct local-network option on a machine that lacks the capability produces a session whose sandboxed commands cannot reach local services. Always false off Windows.
member.param: The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: True when the sandbox on this host can reach host loopback directly.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSandboxApi.GetUnsupportedMessageAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: The explanation a host shows when it refuses an explicit request to turn the sandbox on for a machine that cannot run one. Carries the platform-specific remedy — install bubblewrap, update Windows — and the documentation link, so a host that got `false` from `sandbox.checkPlatformSupport` does not have to compose its own reason and cannot describe the same machine differently from the runtime's own spawn path.
member.param: The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: The user-facing refusal, including the platform remedy and the documentation link.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSandboxApi.GetUnsupportedSettingDisabledNoticeAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: The notice a host shows when a stored `sandbox` setting is being ignored for this session because the machine cannot enforce it. Distinct from `sandbox.getUnsupportedMessage`, which refuses an explicit request: this one reports that a setting the user already saved is inert, states that commands will run unsandboxed, and confirms the stored setting itself is left alone. A host that stays silent here leaves the user believing a sandbox is active.
member.param: The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: The user-facing notice that a saved sandbox setting is inert for this session.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSandboxApi.GetUnsupportedStartupNoticeAsync(System.Object,System.Nullable{System.Boolean},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: The warning a host prints at startup when a session asked for a sandbox on a machine that cannot run one. The third of the unsupported notices, and the only one that depends on the policy in force: it names the remedy the reader can actually act on, which is the stored setting for an unmanaged host, an administrator for a managed one, and waiting for the policy to resolve when the sandbox stayed on only because the policy could not be determined. Returns no notice when the machine does support a sandbox, so a host can call it unconditionally on the startup path. A host that composes its own warning tells a managed user to change a setting their policy will overwrite.
member.param: The managed `sandbox` slice, when a policy supplies one. The notice treats the sandbox as enforced only when this both enables it and sets `failIfUnavailable`, because a managed sandbox that tolerates being unavailable still leaves the user able to turn it off.

True when the sandbox stayed on only because the managed policy could not be determined. Distinguishes a policy that positively enforces the sandbox from one that merely failed to resolve, which is the difference between telling the user to contact an administrator and telling them to wait. Defaults to false.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: The startup warning, absent when the machine can run a sandbox.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSandboxApi.GetPathGrantWarningAsync(System.String,System.Nullable{System.Boolean},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: The warning to show before a user adds a sandbox path grant, when the sandbox backend cannot honor it. On Windows a read/write grant on a drive root such as `C:\` or `V:\` is accepted but gives no access to the files inside it, so the warning steers the user to a specific folder. A read-only grant on a drive root works and gets no warning. The grant is still stored as written: this only advises. Returns no warning on other platforms and for paths that are not a drive root, so a host can call it unconditionally while the user types. A host must ask rather than test the path itself, because which volume shapes the backend honors is a property of the backend, and a host-side check goes stale when it changes.
member.param: The grant as it will reach the sandbox: unquoted, anchored to the session's working directory and normalized. A relative path can give a false negative.
Whether the grant is read-only. Omitted means read/write, which gets the stricter advice.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Advice for a path grant, when it needs any.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSandboxApi.CheckEnforcementCommandAsync(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IList{System.String},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Whether one slash command stays reachable while sandbox enforcement is unavailable and the session is otherwise blocked. The permitted set is deliberately narrow — commands that only report state, and the few that let the user repair or leave the situation — and it is keyed on the arguments as well as the name, so `/sandbox status` is admitted where `/sandbox enable` is not. A host must ask rather than keep its own list: a command this returns false for is one the runtime would refuse anyway, and a divergent list either strands the user with no way out or admits a command that acts on an unenforced session.
member.param: The command name as the user typed it, with or without its leading slash.
The command's arguments, in order. Pass an empty array for a bare command: several entries in the allowlist admit the bare form and refuse every argument.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: True when the command stays available while enforcement is blocked.

member.summary: Returns the documentation URL a host should point a user at when it declines or downgrades a sandbox setting. The runtime owns the address so every surface cites the same page and a host does not hard-code a link that later moves.

member.returns: The documentation URL a host cites when it declines or downgrades a sandbox setting.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerPersistenceApi.WriteRawJsonLockedAsync(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Atomically replaces a JSON file's entire contents while holding the runtime's per-path lock. The lock lives in the runtime process, so a host that writes these files itself takes no part in it and can tear a concurrent runtime write; route the write here instead. Unlike a merging write this never reads or parses the existing file, so a previously corrupted snapshot is replaced wholesale rather than failing every later write. Use it only for callers that always persist a complete snapshot.
member.param: Absolute path of the file to replace. Parent directories are created when missing.
The serialized JSON document to write. It replaces the file's contents entirely; nothing is merged.
Comment lines to emit above the document, for a format that tolerates them. Omit for strict JSON.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: The outcome of a locked snapshot write.

member.summary: Reports whether the gh-replaceable GitHub MCP tools may be clipped for a session, which a host feeds back as the `excludeGhReplaceableTools` build option. The tools are redundant only when the session can reach a shell *and* the host has the `gh` that would replace them, so both halves are decided here. The shell half runs the platform shell tool through the runtime's own tool-filter matcher, so entry forms like `builtin:bash` and `builtin:*` behave exactly as they do when a session builds its tool catalog. The host half probes for `gh`, and is skipped entirely when the filters already rule the shell out. Host presence alone is not enough: a session restricted to, say, `view` would otherwise lose the built-in issue-read fallback while having no shell to replace it with. The answer describes the host the runtime runs on, so it is never forwarded to a remote engine.

A runtime with planning available returns a normalised plan and opaque single-use plan handle; a runtime without it returns the typed planning-unavailable result. A completed plan reports resource identity, provenance, eligible transport choices, the user-scope target, required typed values and secret placeholders, the policy result, the configuration changes installing would make, and whether a reload would be needed. member.summary: Drops the runtime's in-memory cache of discovered custom instructions so the next discovery reads them from disk again. A host calls this after it changes instruction files, or after it trusts a folder whose instructions an earlier discovery skipped, so that a session started afterwards sees the current files instead of a cached earlier answer. The stored credentials are deliberately not part of this result; a caller that needs an authenticated identity asks the account methods for it instead. Reading is non-destructive and every field is optional, because a fresh install has recorded nothing yet.

Use this when a consumer scopes a session to its own Copilot home — the SDK's per-session `configDir` override — so the state read matches the directory that session actually uses. An absent or empty `configDir` resolves the server's own home, making this identical to `globalState.load`. The stored credentials are omitted here for the same reason they are omitted from `globalState.load`: a caller that needs an authenticated identity asks the account methods instead, so pointing this at another directory cannot be used to read the credentials kept in it.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerGlobalStateApi.WriteKeyAsync(System.String,System.String,System.Object,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Records one top-level key in the host's machine-wide state, the counterpart to `globalState.load`. A host calls this to remember that it has shown an onboarding step, asked a one-off question, or completed a migration, so the next run can skip it. Only the named key is replaced and the rest of the document is preserved, which lets two writers record different flags without overwriting each other; passing no value removes the key instead. Only the keys a host records itself are writable: `appTipShown`, `askedSetupTerminals`, `autoFeedbackLastPromptedAt`, `firstLaunchAt`, `recentModelIds`, `sandboxCredentialProxyCaDeclined` and `sandboxOnboardingShown`. Every other key is refused, including `installedPlugins`, the stored credentials, `trustedFolders`, the staff flags and the signed-in accounts. Plugin enablement must use the plugin APIs, which apply repository and managed-policy checks.
member.param: Top-level key to write, named as it appears in the result of `globalState.load`. It must be one of the writable keys that `globalState.writeKey` lists.

Copilot configuration directory to write the state document in, taking precedence over the server's own `COPILOT_HOME` and default home. Omit it, or pass an empty string, to write the directory the server resolved for itself. Mirrors `globalState.loadForConfigDir`, so a caller can read and write the same directory.
Value to store for the key. Omit it, or pass null, to remove the key instead.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .

With `resolveProxy`, the client decides the proxies for every request the runtime would otherwise route by ambient proxy settings (proxy environment variables, `NO_PROXY` and operating-system settings), or leaves a request to that routing; requests with an explicitly configured proxy and loopback targets never consult it. With `authenticateNegotiate`, the client supplies the Kerberos tokens for Negotiate proxy challenges instead of native credential lookup. The callbacks serve requests made for the client's sessions and, with `runtime` scope, the runtime's shared traffic, which includes background requests and remote MCP server connections; only one connection may hold `runtime` scope. The registration ends when the connection closes.
member.param: Traffic the callbacks serve; defaults to `connection`.
Present when the client answers `network.resolveProxy`.
Present when the client answers `network.authenticateNegotiate`.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSessionsApi.ReadPersistedEventsAsync(System.String,System.String,System.Nullable{System.Int64},System.Nullable{GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventsReadDirection},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Reads a page of durable events directly from a local session's persisted journal without creating, resuming, or activating the session. The first read pins the currently opened journal generation and its byte-length boundary; opaque cursor continuations remain on that generation across runtime-owned compaction, truncation, and rewrite operations, which replace the live path atomically, and events appended after the boundary are excluded. For cold hydration, await the first successful page before activation and establish lossless live-event buffering before resume; merge subsequent live events by ID, preserving persisted order and letting live payloads win. Continuations are process-local, single-use capabilities bound to the originating session and storage context and must be paged sequentially; concurrent or repeated use of the same cursor expires that duplicate read rather than reading the generation twice. A complete snapshot has cursorStatus 'ok' and hasMore false. Snapshots expire after five idle minutes, with at most eight retained per process and idle-only eviction under pressure; completion and cancelled-worker exit release their handles. No transcript copy is created, but retained handles may keep replaced files' disk blocks alive until release. Pages have a soft 1 MiB serialized event-array budget including resolved binary assets; one oversized event is returned alone to guarantee progress. Working memory also includes a record/lookahead and asset resolution; resolving the first binary reference may scan the full pinned generation to build a bounded offset index. If the snapshot expires, is evicted, is cancelled before a continuation is established, or becomes unreadable after an observable unsupported in-place shortening, the continuation returns cursorStatus 'expired' with an empty terminal page and never falls back to a different generation. A missing or initially unreadable journal is an RPC error. Persisted history excludes ephemeral events and may omit payloads that are reconstructed only for an active session; use the active session event stream for post-resume live events.
member.param: Session ID whose persisted event journal should be read.

Opaque, process-local, single-use cursor returned by the previous persisted-event read. Omit on the first call and issue continuations sequentially; reusing the same cursor returns an expired terminal page.

Maximum number of events to return in this batch (1–1000, default 200). Pages may contain fewer events to keep the serialized event array within a soft 1 MiB budget including resolved binary assets; one oversized event is returned alone to guarantee progress.

Direction to page through persisted history. Forward starts at the beginning; backward starts with the newest events. Events in each page remain chronological. This selects the initial read only; a continuation always uses the direction bound into its cursor.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Batch of session events returned by a read, with cursor and continuation metadata.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerSessionsApi.CreateWorkspaceAsync(System.String,System.String,System.String,GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.SessionWorkingDirectoryContextWithClient,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Creates the workspace record for a session that has not been opened yet. A host that hands a session off to another application — writing the record and then launching that application against the session ID — needs the record on disk before any session exists to carry it, which the session-scoped workspace methods cannot do. Replaces any existing record and resets the checkpoint index. When writing to the local filesystem, a stored `fork_count` survives on disk. Returns the record it built, so a surviving stored `fork_count` can differ from the answer.
member.param: Session ID the workspace record belongs to.
Directory the session's state is written under when no session filesystem provider is configured. Ignored when a provider is configured; the provider's session state path is used instead.
`windows` (any letter case) selects Windows path rules. Any other value selects POSIX path rules.

Starting working-directory context. The record keeps `cwd`, `gitRoot`, `repository`, `hostType`, `branch`, and `clientName`. Other fields, including `repositoryHost`, `headCommit`, and `baseCommit`, are ignored. `hostType` must be `github` or `ado`.
User-supplied display name for the workspace.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: The workspace record that was written.

Resuming by session ID has to know where the session lives before it can connect, so the lookup cannot come from the session-scoped workspace methods, which resolve their location from a live session's context. Returns no record when the file is absent.
member.param: Root directory every session's state directory sits under.
Session ID naming the state directory under the sessions home. Rejected when it is absolute or contains a parent component, so it cannot escape the sessions home.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: The workspace record on disk, omitted when the session has none.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerTaskAnalyticsApi
member.summary: Provides server-scoped TaskAnalytics APIs.

Classifies a recorded Copilot or ATIF trajectory using the runtime's production analytics pipeline. No conversation session is required or created, archived tools are never executed, and classification telemetry is not emitted. Calling this method explicitly requests model processing of retained trajectory content through the connection's GitHub CAPI credentials, independently of background telemetry consent; BYOK endpoints are not used. Callers must authorize that processing and validate archive provenance. Content is not automatically redacted or sanitized for prompt injection. Model-derived results can be manipulated by trajectory content and must not be used as authorization or security decisions.
member.param: Canonical Copilot session event objects or ATIF step objects, in source order, starting at the beginning of the recorded conversation. An ATIF document containing steps can be passed as a single array element. Include source identifiers when present. Durable Copilot logs are accepted; abort events retain interruptions, and EOF closes an unfinished turn without claiming successful completion. Non-analytics event types are ignored. Treat the archive as untrusted input: this API does not authenticate its origin, roles, completion claims, or content. Callers must validate provenance and preserve event structure, ordering, and role/source metadata. Remove or redact secrets and personal data that must not be sent to GitHub CAPI before calling; automatic redaction and prompt-injection sanitization are not provided. Retained text is bounded, not made trustworthy. Adversarial instructions can bias model judgments just as in live conversations; stripping instruction-like text is not required and can change the evidence being measured.
Classifier names to run. Omit for all eight classifiers. An empty list runs none. Turn splitting is also returned when needed to build task/session units or identify task-opening turns.

Maximum concurrent classifier calls in this analysis across all lanes, including segmentation and session classifiers. Defaults to 4; must be positive. Multiple simultaneous analyses each have their own limit. Trajectory concurrency is not inference-request concurrency.

Explicit judge configuration for this analysis. Omit to use each classifier's production model policy and reasoning effort. The exact model must be offered by the authenticated catalog, allowed by server policy, and compatible with the classifier; an unusable override fails the affected classification rather than falling back. Choosing a billed model explicitly authorizes its inference costs. Successful rows reused from previousResult keep their original judge configuration.

Validate input locally without authentication, model discovery, or inference. Returns validation diagnostics and no classifications. Invalid input never starts paid inference, even when this option is omitted.

Previous result for the identical archive and classifier versions. Reuses all original task boundaries, including unresolved ones, and preserves successful and declined outcomes. Only failed/abandoned non-segmenting outcomes in the selected classifiers are retried. Start a fresh analysis to change segmentation. Rejects mismatched fingerprints or versions before inference.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Categorical retrospective measurements of the supplied trajectory, not verification that its claims are true. Model-derived classifications can be inaccurate or manipulated by adversarial content. Treat them as untrusted measurements; independently validate results used for consequential decisions and never use them as authorization or security decisions.

member.summary: Starts a cloud coding-agent task, the remote run whose record `cloudTasks.get` later reads. Answered above any session because the task it creates is not a background task inside one. Hosts other than the CLI want this: a GitHub App or an SDK consumer that hands work to a cloud agent creates the same task under the same credential, and resolving it here keeps one credential, endpoint and validation path. Target the task either by repository, supplying both `repositoryOwner` and `repositoryName`, or by `owner` alone for an account-level run. The result separates a rejected request from a failed one: when `ok` is false, `reason` categorises the rejection and `message` carries the explanation to show, while `failure` describes the HTTP call itself and is present only when one was actually made.
member.param: The credential the task is created under, carried opaquely because its shape is the host's own and the runtime only resolves a token and an API endpoint from it.
Name of the embedding client, reported to the service so it can attribute the request.
Explicit Mission Control endpoint selected by the host. Omission derives it from the identity.
Selects which stored credential to resolve when the host holds more than one. Omit it to resolve the default for the supplied `authInfo`.
Account or organization owning the repository the task runs against. Supply it together with `repositoryName`.
Name of the repository the task runs against. Supply it together with `repositoryOwner`.
Account the task is created for when it is not tied to a repository. Supply it only when `repositoryOwner` and `repositoryName` are omitted.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: The outcome of starting a cloud task. A rejected request and a failed one are reported separately: `reason` and `message` describe a request the service declined, while `statusCode` and `errorMessage` describe the HTTP call itself and appear only when one was actually made.

member.summary: Deletes one cloud coding-agent task, the remote run `cloudTasks.create` started. The deletion is a soft one: the service withdraws the task from its listings rather than destroying the record, so a host removing a run from its own UI is the intended caller. Answered above any session for the same reason as `cloudTasks.get` -- the task is remote and has no local counterpart. Hosts other than the CLI want this: a GitHub App or an SDK consumer that manages cloud agent runs withdraws the same record under the same credential, and resolving it here keeps one credential-resolution and endpoint path. The runtime resolves each token from `authInfo` or `authContextId`. A host may preserve an explicit `baseUrl`; omission derives the endpoint from `authInfo`. The result is the HTTP outcome rather than a bare success flag: the call returns no body, so `ok` alone describes a success, while a failure is reported through `statusCode`, `errorMessage` and `errorPayloadJson` instead of being raised as an error.
member.param: The credential the deletion is performed under, carried opaquely because its shape is the host's own and the runtime only resolves a token and an API endpoint from it. Required: the task endpoint is per-account, so there is no unauthenticated form of this call.
Name of the embedding client, reported to Mission Control so the service can attribute the request.
Identifier of the cloud task to delete.
Explicit Mission Control endpoint selected by the host. Omission derives it from the identity.
Selects which stored credential to resolve when the host holds more than one. Omit it to resolve the default for the supplied `authInfo`.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: The HTTP outcome of deleting a cloud task. The deletion returns no body, so a successful call carries nothing beyond `ok`; a failed one is described by the remaining fields rather than raised as an error, so a caller can surface the service's own explanation.

This is the task a cloud agent runs on a host's behalf, not a background task inside a session, so it is answered above any session and the `tasks` group does not cover it. Hosts other than the CLI want this: a GitHub App or an SDK consumer that shows the state of a cloud agent run must read the same task record, and resolving it here keeps one credential-resolution, task-URL and circuit-breaker path instead of each host rebuilding them. The result is the HTTP outcome rather than the task itself: a caller must read `ok` and `statusCode` before `payloadJson`, because a 404 is reported as a non-ok result rather than an error, which is what lets a caller tell "no such task" apart from "the API call failed".

Answered above any session, for the same reason as `cloudTasks.get`: the session being asked about runs remotely and has no local counterpart. Read `resolved` first. Hosts other than the CLI want this: an SDK consumer attaching to a run in progress, an ACP client resuming one, or a GitHub App rendering a task's transcript all rebuild the same history from the same events, and resolving it here keeps one credential, endpoint, ordering and anchor-detection path. member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ServerCloudTasksApi.ResolveTaskIdAsync(System.String,System.Object,System.String,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Collections.Generic.IList{System.String},System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Finds the session a caller should open for one cloud coding-agent task. A task identifier alone does not say what to open: the run may already exist locally, it may exist only in the cloud, or it may be a task that cannot be resumed at all. Resolving that needs a local session scan and a Mission Control lookup that agree on identity, which is why it is answered here rather than left to each host. Hosts other than the CLI want it: an IDE or a GitHub App that opens a run from a task link faces the same three outcomes. Read `kind` before any other field. `local-session` carries `sessionId`, `remote-session` carries `metadataJson`, `unresumable-task` means the task exists but cannot be continued, and `none` means no session matched. A failed service call is reported as `error` rather than raised, so a caller can surface the service's own message. Pass every local session identifier already rejected in `ignoredLocalSessionIds` and call again to get the next candidate; that is how a host skips a local session it could not load.
member.param: Identifier of the cloud task to resolve.

The credential the lookup is performed under, carried opaquely because its shape is the host's own and the runtime only resolves a token and an API endpoint from it. Required: the task endpoint is per-account, so there is no unauthenticated form of this call.

member.summary: Sends a user message to the session and returns its message ID.
member.param: The user message text.
If provided, this is shown in the timeline instead of `prompt`.
Optional attachments (files, directories, selections, blobs, GitHub references) to include with the message.
How to deliver the message. `enqueue` (default) appends to the message queue. `immediate` interjects during an in-progress turn.
If true, adds the message to the front of the queue instead of the end.
If false, this message will not trigger a Premium Request Unit charge. User messages default to billable.
If set, the request will fail if the named tool is not available when this message is among the user messages at the start of the current exchange.

Optional provenance tag copied to the resulting user.message event. Must be `user`, `system`, `command-<command-id>` for command-originated messages, `schedule-<numeric-id>` for scheduled prompts, `agent-<agent-id>` for prompts sent by another agent, or `automation-<automation-id>` for turns a host sends on behalf of an automation the user configured. An automation turn defines the session's task like a user message but carries no human authority.
The UI mode the agent was in when this message was sent. Defaults to the session's current mode.
Custom HTTP headers to include in outbound model requests for this turn. Merged with session-level provider headers; per-turn headers augment and overwrite session-level headers with the same key.

Provider-native output format for this turn, including all tool-call iterations. Not inherited by later turns or subagents. Ordinary steering inherits the active format; specifying responseFormat with mode: immediate is an error, even while idle. Returned assistant content remains text; the runtime does not parse or validate it. Unsupported models or schemas produce provider errors.
W3C Trace Context traceparent header for distributed tracing of this agent turn.
W3C Trace Context tracestate header for distributed tracing.

If true, await completion of the agentic loop for this message before returning. Defaults to false (fire-and-forget). When true, the result still contains the same `messageId`; the caller can rely on the agent having processed the message before the call resolves. Transport-dependent tail semantics: on a LOCAL (in-process) session the wait additionally blocks until the completed turn's event tail has been dispatched to this session's in-process subscribers, so a subsequent read of subscriber state already reflects the turn; on a REMOTE session the wait resolves once the loop completes and mirrored delivery follows over the wire. Callers that need the stronger local guarantee on remote sessions should await the event stream explicitly.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Result of sending a user message.

When true, defer this switch (enqueue it) if another model change is already queued, even when no turn is active — so it drains last (FIFO) and wins over the already-queued change. Intended for genuine user-initiated model selections; internal restore/reapply switches omit it and apply immediately when no turn is active. When no other model change is queued this has no effect (a switch still applies immediately unless a turn is active).
Explicit response to a model-switch compaction preflight. Omit to request a confirmation projection when compaction is necessary.

When true, evaluate context-window compaction policy before applying the switch, including effort-only and unchanged selections while idle. An effort-only change applies immediately without compaction when a turn is active, including when the turn starts during preflight; an explicit `compactionDecision: "cancel"` still cancels the change. Other switches retain preflight and may be deferred until the active turn ends.

member.summary: Adds BYOK providers and/or models to the session's registry at runtime, extending the additive registry built from the session's `providers`/`models` options. Both fields are optional, so a call may add providers only, models only, or both. Within a single call providers are registered before models, so a model may reference a provider added in the same call; across calls a model may reference any provider already registered (from session creation or a prior add). A model whose referenced provider is not registered by the end of the call is rejected. Newly added models become selectable via `model.list` / `model.switchTo` and are inherited by sub-agents spawned afterwards.
member.param: Named BYOK provider connections to register, additive to any providers already in the registry. Each name must be unique across the registry and must not contain '/'.
BYOK model definitions to register. Each must reference a provider that is already registered or included in this same call. Selection ids (`provider/id`) must be unique across the registry.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: The selectable model entries synthesized for the models added by this call.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ProviderApi.WithdrawAsync(System.Collections.Generic.IList{System.String},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Withdraws named host-managed models from the session's BYOK registry, leaving every other entry untouched. The scoped counterpart to `provider.sync`: a snapshot can only describe entries the caller knows about, so using it to remove one model silently withdraws rows registered by another source, such as a plugin calling `provider.add` at runtime. Naming what to remove leaves unrelated entries alone. Selection ids that are not registered are ignored, so withdrawal is idempotent. A provider is removed only when one of the withdrawn models was the last entry referencing it; a provider that simply has no models, which is the normal state while its rows are supplied by catalog discovery, is left in place.
member.param: Provider-qualified selection ids to withdraw. Ids that are not registered are ignored, so withdrawal is idempotent. A provider left with no models referencing it is removed too.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: What the withdrawal actually removed from the registry.

member.summary: Host-only reconciliation of authoritative session-effective extension membership and enablement. Refreshes runtime-owned discovery and preferences without persisting settings, installing plugins, or restarting unchanged activations. Returns ExtensionList only after required starts and process/contribution cleanup settle. Takes no caller inventory or overrides. Missing controllers, unready/incomplete discovery, unavailable workspaces, superseded inputs, and lifecycle failures are errors, not empty membership. Independently proven revocations may be applied before an error; retry converges without restarting healthy activations. Error data contains lifecycleChangesApplied and code: extension_reconciliation_host_required, extension_reconciliation_unavailable, extension_reconciliation_not_ready, extension_reconciliation_discovery_failed, extension_reconciliation_workspace_unavailable, extension_reconciliation_superseded, or extension_reconciliation_lifecycle_failed. Mark host reconciliation state applied only on success. On older runtimes, method-not-found must not fall back to global discovery and persistent extension disables.
member.param: The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Extensions discovered for the session, with their current status.

member.summary: Records a working-directory/git context change and emits a `session.context_changed` event. For a local session, a report whose `cwd` diverges from the session's current working directory is ignored (the call still succeeds but records nothing and emits no event): a local session's working directory is authoritative and is moved via `metadata.setWorkingDirectory` (or an SDK `session.resume` that supplies a `workingDirectory`), not by this method.
member.param: Updated working directory and git context. Emitted as the new payload of `session.context_changed`.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Notify the session that its working directory context has changed. Emits a `session.context_changed` event so consumers (telemetry, OTel tracker, ACP, the timeline UI) can react. Use this when the host has detected a cwd/branch/repo change outside the session's normal lifecycle (e.g., after a shell command in interactive mode). For a local session, a report whose `cwd` diverges from the session's current working directory is ignored (the call still succeeds but records nothing and emits no event); move a local session's working directory via `metadata.setWorkingDirectory` instead.

member.summary: Updates the session's working directory. For local sessions the target is validated first (an absolute path that exists on disk) and the permission primary directory is re-based; a rejected validation fails the call before any session state changes.
member.param: Absolute path to set as the session's working directory. The runtime updates the session's recorded cwd so subsequent operations (shell tools, file lookups, telemetry) anchor to it.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Update the session's working directory. Used by the host when the user explicitly changes cwd (e.g., the `/cd` slash command). The host is responsible for any related side-effects (file index, etc.); it does NOT change the process working directory (a session's cwd is per-session, not process-global). For local sessions the runtime validates the target first (an absolute path that exists on disk) and re-bases the permission primary directory; a rejected validation fails the call before anything is mutated, persisted, or emitted. Location-scoped permission rules are then re-keyed to the new directory (best-effort). Remote sessions only record the path.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ShellApi.ExecAsync(System.String,System.String,System.Nullable{System.TimeSpan},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Starts a shell command, returning an RPC error if it cannot be spawned. The command runs as the leader of its own process group (POSIX) or in a dedicated job object (Windows), so a forced termination — via "shell.kill", the request timeout, or session disposal — signals that whole group/job rather than only the direct child. Two gaps are worth planning for: a command that exits on its own does not trigger that teardown, and on POSIX a descendant that moves itself into a new session or process group (for example via "setsid") leaves the signalled group, so either can leave a background process running.
member.param: Shell command to execute.
Working directory (defaults to session working directory).
Timeout in milliseconds (default: 30000).
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Identifier of the spawned shell process, usable with shell.kill while the process is running.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ShellApi.KillAsync(System.String,System.Nullable{GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ShellKillSignal},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Sends a signal to a shell process previously started via "shell.exec". The signal targets the command's whole process group (POSIX) or job object (Windows), so descendants still in that group are signalled too, not just the direct child. On POSIX a descendant that moved itself into a new session or process group (for example via "setsid") is no longer in the signalled group and survives.
member.param: Process identifier returned by shell.exec.
Signal to send (default: SIGTERM).
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Indicates whether the signal was delivered; false if the process was unknown or already exited.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HistoryApi.RewindAsync(System.String,GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HistoryRewindMode,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Rewinds the session conversation, optionally restoring files changed by the discarded turns. Not crash-atomic: file restore and conversation truncation are separate stores, applied in that order, so a process crash between them can leave the workspace rewound while the conversation still contains the discarded turns. There is no recovery journal; re-running the same rewind is the recovery path for a crash before truncation lands, since file restore is idempotent (already-restored files are reported as skipped) and truncation is re-derived from the still-retained boundary event. After truncation lands that boundary no longer exists, so the same request is rejected; the only stage that can still be outstanding is snapshot pruning, whose failure leaves orphan snapshots the capture store tolerates. The reverse inconsistency cannot occur, because truncation is never applied before file restore succeeds.
member.param: ID of the user.message event that begins the discarded suffix.
Whether to rewind only conversation history or also restore captured files.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Structured outcome of a rewind request.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.HistoryApi.SetCompactionConfigAsync(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Replaces this local session's compaction settings: the model, prompt and reasoning effort its automatic and manual compactions use. Each call replaces all three: an omitted field returns to its default. Settings are held in memory only, so re-apply them after resuming the session in a new process. A change applies to compactions that start afterwards, except that automatic compactions keep the model the running turn already chose for them until that turn ends; a compaction already in progress may still pick up a new reasoning effort. Rejects on a remote session.
member.param: Model that summarizes this session's conversation when it compacts, instead of the session's own model. Applies only when both are Copilot models the session may use; for a BYOK or provider session, or a model the session's catalog or allowed-model policy rejects, compaction summarizes on the session's model. Takes precedence over any runtime experiment that picks a compaction model. Blank values are ignored.

Summarization instruction sent as the final user message of a compaction request, replacing the built-in prompt entirely; the caller owns the summary's format. `/compact` focus instructions and a note that tools are unavailable are appended to it. Blank values are ignored.

Reasoning effort for compaction requests: one of `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Applies when the model that summarizes supports it; otherwise the request keeps its usual effort. Takes precedence over any runtime experiment that adjusts compaction reasoning effort. Any other value is rejected.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EventLogApi
member.summary: Provides session-scoped EventLog APIs.
Reads a batch of session events from a cursor, optionally waiting for new events. Supports tail-first reads via `direction: backward`.
member.param: Opaque cursor returned by a previous read in the same view. Omit on the first call to start from the beginning of the selected view.
Maximum number of events to return in this batch (1–1000, default 200).

Milliseconds to wait for new events when the cursor is at the tail of history. 0 (default) returns immediately even if no events are available. Capped at 30000ms. Ephemeral events that arrive during the wait are delivered in this batch but are NOT replayable on a subsequent read (use a non-zero waitMs in your next call to capture future ephemerals as they happen). This applies to forward reads only: a backward read always returns immediately and ignores `waitMs`, because backward paging covers persisted history only while new events append at the tail (the opposite end from a backward page), so no blocking or ephemeral delivery can occur.
Either '*' to receive all event types, or a non-empty list of event types to receive.

Agent-scope filter: 'primary' returns only main-agent events plus events whose type starts with 'subagent.' (matching the typed-subscription default behavior); 'all' returns events from all agents (matching wildcard-subscription behavior). Default is 'all' to preserve wildcard semantics for catch-up callers.

Optional non-empty list of subagent identifiers. When provided, only events owned by one of these agents are returned; ownership recognizes the event envelope's agentId plus legacy data.agentId and data.parentToolCallId markers. This filter takes precedence over agentScope.

Direction to page through the session's persisted event history. 'forward' (default) pages from the cursor toward newer events (or from the start of history when no cursor is given). 'backward' enables tail-first reads: with no cursor it returns the NEWEST `max` events, and the returned cursor pages toward OLDER events on subsequent backward reads. Events within a returned batch are always in chronological (oldest-to-newest) order, even for a backward read. Backward reads cover PERSISTED history only; ephemeral events are never returned by a backward read. `direction` selects the INITIAL read only: the returned cursor is self-describing, so a continuation read pages in the cursor's own direction regardless of the `direction` passed alongside it — a forward cursor always pages forward and a backward cursor always pages backward. Pass the direction that matches the cursor to avoid confusion.

When false, skip ephemeral events entirely and return only durable (persisted) events. History-backfill callers that discard ephemerals anyway should set this so the read is bounded by the durable log length instead of racing the ephemeral ring on a busy session. Defaults to true (ephemerals are interleaved with durable events in creation order). Ignored by backward reads, which always cover persisted history only.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Batch of session events returned by a read, with cursor and continuation metadata.

member.summary: Registers consumer interest in an event type for runtime gating purposes.
member.param: The event type the consumer wants the runtime to treat as 'observed' for behavior-switching gating. Some runtime code paths inspect whether any consumer is interested in a specific event type and choose a different implementation accordingly (e.g. `mcp.oauth_required`: when interest is registered the runtime delegates interactive OAuth token acquisition to the consumer via `mcp.oauth_required` events; when no interest is registered the runtime still attempts non-interactive reconnect from cached or refreshable tokens, and only marks the server `needs-auth` if usable credentials are unavailable — it does not open a browser or start interactive OAuth without a consumer). SDK clients that long-poll events do NOT automatically appear as listeners to these gating checks — they must explicitly call `registerInterest` for each event type they want the runtime to count as having a consumer. Multiple registrations for the same event type from the same or different consumers are tracked independently and must each be released. See: `mcp.oauth_required`, `sampling.requested`, `auto_mode_switch.requested`, `session_limits_exhausted.requested`, `user_input.requested`, `elicitation.requested`, `command.queued`, `exit_plan_mode.requested`.

member.summary: Handles `extensionLaunchProvider` client global API methods.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.IExtensionLaunchProviderHandler.ResolveAsync(GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ExtensionLaunchProviderResolveRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Asks the registered SDK client to resolve an opaque process launch profile for one discovered extension entrypoint immediately before launch or reload. The provider must respond within 15 seconds.
member.param: A discovered extension entrypoint that the registered integrator may classify and resolve to an opaque launch profile.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: The launch profile for a supported entrypoint. Omit launch when the provider does not support the entrypoint.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.INetworkHandler
member.summary: Handles `network` client global API methods.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.INetworkHandler.ResolveProxyAsync(GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.NetworkResolveProxyRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Requests the proxies for a request target as a PAC-style proxy list, or no list to leave the request to the runtime's own proxy resolution. The runtime caches answers for a few seconds and fails the request, rather than connecting directly, when the callback fails.
member.param: Requests the proxies for a request target.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Proxies for a request target, in the order to try them.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.INetworkHandler.AuthenticateNegotiateAsync(GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.NetworkAuthenticateNegotiateRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Requests a fresh base64 initial SPNEGO token for a Kerberos service principal; the runtime uses it to answer Negotiate proxy challenges. Tokens must not be logged, persisted or reused across connections. Continuation challenges are not supported by this callback.
member.param: Requests a fresh initial SPNEGO token for a Kerberos service principal.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Client credentials for a single Negotiate authentication exchange.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ILlmInferenceHandler
member.summary: Handles `llmInference` client global API methods.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ILlmInferenceHandler.HttpRequestStartAsync(GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.LlmInferenceHttpRequestStartRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Announces an outbound model-layer HTTP request the runtime wants the SDK client to service. Carries the request head only; the body always follows as one or more httpRequestChunk frames keyed by the same requestId, even when the body is empty (a single chunk with end=true).
member.param: The head of an outbound model-layer HTTP request.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Acknowledgement. Returning successfully simply means the SDK accepted the start frame; it does not imply the request will succeed.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.ILlmInferenceHandler.HttpRequestChunkAsync(GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.LlmInferenceHttpRequestChunkRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Delivers a body byte range (or a cancellation signal) for a request previously announced via httpRequestStart, correlated by requestId. The runtime fires at least one chunk per request — when there is no body, a single chunk with empty data and end=true. Mid-stream the runtime may send a chunk with cancel=true to abort the request; the SDK then stops issuing httpResponseChunk frames and may emit a terminal httpResponseChunk with error set.
member.param: A request body chunk or cancellation signal.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Acknowledgement. The SDK is free to ignore the ack and treat chunk delivery as fire-and-forget.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.IGitHubTelemetryHandler
member.summary: Handles `gitHubTelemetry` client global API methods.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.IGitHubTelemetryHandler.EventAsync(GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.GitHubTelemetryNotification,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Forwards a single GitHub telemetry event to a host connection that opted into telemetry forwarding during the `server.connect` handshake. Opted-in connections receive their runtime host's events across all its sessions, its sessionless events (for example, `server.sendTelemetry`), and explicitly process-wide events. Events owned by another independently embedded runtime host are not forwarded to this connection.
member.param: Payload for a `gitHubTelemetry.event` notification: a single GitHub telemetry event the runtime forwards to a host connection that opted into telemetry forwarding during the `server.connect` handshake.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.IGitHubTokenHandler
member.summary: Handles `gitHubToken` client global API methods.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.IGitHubTokenHandler.GetTokenAsync(GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.GitHubTokenAcquireRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Asks the SDK client to mint a GitHub access token for a session whose configuration supplied a GitHub token provider. The runtime acquires the initial token during bootstrap and refreshes it during expiry preflight when one hour or less remains.
member.param: Asks the SDK client to acquire a GitHub access token from an opaque callback registration.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: SDK host response to a GitHub credential request.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.IEntraTokenHandler
member.summary: Handles `entraToken` client global API methods.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.IEntraTokenHandler.GetTokenAsync(GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.EntraTokenGetTokenRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Asks this connection's host-owned Entra provider to select or revalidate an identity, or acquire a token for the pinned identity and requested resource. Standard JSON-RPC cancellation and connection closure retire acquisition; late responses cannot establish credentials.
member.param: Parameters for one connection-owned Entra acquisition callback.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: Host response to Entra acquisition. Unavailable, cancellation and errors are terminal: the runtime must not substitute another account or sign-in transport.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.IUiThreadHandler
member.summary: Handles `uiThread` client global API methods.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.IUiThreadHandler.RunAsync(GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.UiThreadRunRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Schedules a runtime-owned native action through an in-process SDK host's runOnUiThread callback. The SDK supplies an action that enters the native C ABI synchronously; the host executes it exactly once on its UI thread (the process main thread on macOS) and completes only after it returns. Never sent to out-of-process clients.
member.param: Identifies one runtime-owned native action for an in-process SDK UI dispatcher.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.IInstallationsHandler
member.summary: Handles `installations` client global API methods.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.IInstallationsHandler.ConfirmAsync(GitHub.Copilot.Rpc.InstallationsConfirmRequest,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Requests a fresh explicit human decision for one sealed installation operation on its original connection. Present the complete typed review, return the original challenge and fingerprint, and never infer approval. The expiresAt deadline, connection closure or standard JSON-RPC $/cancelRequest retires the request; late replies grant no authority.
member.param: One connection-owned, expiring request for a trusted host's explicit user decision.
The to monitor for cancellation requests. The default is .
member.returns: A response is meaningful only on the connection and request that issued its challenge.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.SessionModelDeselectedEvent
member.summary: The model the user had explicitly selected is no longer available, because the host that published it withdrew it, so the session no longer has an explicit selection. The next turn resolves a default as though the user had never chosen a model. Clients should stop presenting the previous model as selected. This event is durable because resume rebuilds the selected model from the event log; without it a resumed session would restore a model its provider no longer serves. Reasoning effort, verbosity, and other session-level preferences are deliberately unchanged, because they belong to the session rather than to the model.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.SessionAutoModeResolvedEvent
member.summary: Auto Intent resolution: the concrete model an auto-mode session settled on, and why. Published when Auto settles on a model that differs from the one it last published in the current Auto selection, so a routing check that keeps the same model does not repeat it; selecting a model, switching Auto tiers, or returning to Auto starts a new selection. Lets SDK clients render the chosen model and the full reason it was picked. The core selection fields (chosenModel/reasoningBucket/categoryScores) are stable; the routing-analytics fields (predictedLabel/confidence/candidateModels) mirror the upstream intent service and may evolve, hence the event's experimental stability.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedEvent
member.summary: Effective enterprise managed settings and contributing channels. Session events report applied policy; sessionless resolve reports an account/device snapshot, and compose reports a non-applying preview of candidate documents. Device values take precedence over server values, then the policy helper, per ordinary key, while permissions compose restrictively. Session-local SDK-client policy is included only in session results. Marked experimental while the managed-settings surface stabilizes.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedEvent.Data
member.summary: The session.managed_settings_resolved event payload.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsEnforcedEvent
member.summary: Runtime enforcement of enterprise managed settings: fires when the session blocks or caps a runtime action because enterprise policy governs it, so SDK clients can explain *why* an action was governed. Unlike `session.managed_settings_resolved` (which reports *what* is managed), this reports a concrete governed action — e.g. a user or host tried to turn on bypass permissions or Assisted Permissions while the corresponding policy disables it. Emitted live (not persisted to the session event log) on user/host-initiated attempts only, never for silent policy application. Marked experimental while the managed-settings surface stabilizes.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.EligibleForAutoSwitch
member.summary: Only set on `errorType: "rate_limit"`. When `true`, the runtime will follow this error with an `auto_mode_switch.requested` event (or silently switch if `continueOnAutoMode` is enabled). UI clients can use this flag to suppress duplicate rendering of the rate-limit error when they show their own auto-mode-switch prompt.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.ErrorCode
member.summary: Fine-grained error code from the upstream provider, when available. For `errorType: "rate_limit"`, this is one of the `RateLimitErrorCode` values (e.g., `"user_weekly_rate_limited"`, `"user_global_rate_limited"`, `"rate_limited"`, `"user_model_rate_limited"`, `"integration_rate_limited"`). For `errorType: "quota"`, this is the CAPI quota error code (e.g., `"quota_exceeded"`, `"session_quota_exceeded"`, `"billing_not_configured"`).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.ErrorType
member.summary: Category of error (e.g., "authentication", "authorization", "policy", "quota", "rate_limit", "context_limit", "query").

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.Message
member.summary: Human-readable error message.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.OriginatingMessageId
member.summary: Original root user-message ID of the failed request, including failures before user.message is emitted. Absent for session-wide errors or legacy hosts.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.ProviderCallId
member.summary: GitHub request tracing ID (x-github-request-id header) for correlating with server-side logs.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.ProviderErrorCode
member.summary: Provider-defined error code, when available; unset otherwise. Unlike errorCode, this is not a runtime or Copilot API classification and does not imply a remediation or retry policy.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.ProviderErrorParam
member.summary: Sanitized provider-defined error parameter preserved from a structured upstream error envelope, when available.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.ProviderErrorType
member.summary: Provider-defined error type preserved from a structured upstream error envelope, when available (for example, `invalid_request_error`).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.Remediation
member.summary: What the user must do to recover, when the runtime knows of an action. The `message` never names a client affordance, so a client that offers one — a slash command, a settings pane, a link — renders it from this value.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.ServiceRequestId
member.summary: Copilot service request ID (x-copilot-service-request-id header) for CAPI log correlation.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.Stack

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.StatusCode

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionErrorData.Url

member.summary: Scheduled prompt registered via /every or /after.

member.summary: Absolute fire time (epoch milliseconds) for a one-shot calendar schedule.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionScheduleCreatedData.Cron
member.summary: 5-field cron expression for a recurring calendar schedule, evaluated in `tz`.

member.summary: Optional user-facing label shown in the timeline instead of the actual prompt (e.g. `/skill-name args` when the prompt is a skill invocation expansion).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionScheduleCreatedData.Id
member.summary: Sequential id assigned to the scheduled prompt within the session.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionScheduleCreatedData.Interval
member.summary: Interval between ticks in milliseconds (relative-interval schedules).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionScheduleCreatedData.Origin
member.summary: Who created the schedule (`user` or `model`). Persisted so a resumed session keeps gating non-user schedules from firing skills that opted out of model invocation. Absent on entries created before this field existed; a missing origin fails closed (treated the same as a non-user origin), so such a schedule may not resolve a `disable-model-invocation` skill.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionScheduleCreatedData.Prompt
member.summary: Prompt text that gets enqueued on every tick.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionScheduleCreatedData.Recurring
member.summary: Whether the schedule re-arms after each tick (`/every`) or fires once (`/after`).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionScheduleCreatedData.SelfPaced
member.summary: True for a self-paced (`dynamic`) schedule: no fixed cadence; the model arms each next run via the `manage_schedule` `wakeup` action. `nextRunAt` is model-controlled rather than auto-computed.

member.summary: Reason the change happened, when not user-initiated. `"rate_limit_auto_switch"` for changes triggered by the auto-mode-switch rate-limit recovery path, `"auto_mode_recovery"` when a prepared Auto route commits and a recovered inference is allowed to proceed before provider dispatch, or `"refusal_fallback"` when the active model declined a request (content refusal) and the runtime switched to the configured refusal-fallback model. member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.SessionModelDeselectedData
member.summary: The model the user had explicitly selected is no longer available, because the host that published it withdrew it, so the session no longer has an explicit selection. The next turn resolves a default as though the user had never chosen a model. Clients should stop presenting the previous model as selected. This event is durable because resume rebuilds the selected model from the event log; without it a resumed session would restore a model its provider no longer serves. Reasoning effort, verbosity, and other session-level preferences are deliberately unchanged, because they belong to the session rather than to the model.

member.summary: Model that was selected before the host withdrew it.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionModelDeselectedData.Reason
member.summary: Low-cardinality reason the selection was cleared.

member.summary: Logical ID of the primary user message that initiated this run, matching the messageId returned by session.send (or the last messageId of session.sendMessages). Stable across model/tool iterations, steering messages, and stop-hook corrections. Subagent runs use their own initiating message ID, not the parent's. Absent for runs without an associated initiating message, such as empty batches.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.AssistantMessageData.ProviderId
member.summary: Opaque origin provider identity captured at dispatch. Only an exact match with the target provider permits replay of reasoningOpaque, encryptedContent, reasoningBlocks, serverTools, and provider response/item identifiers. Matching model ids or wire protocols is insufficient. Omitted for legacy or unattributed messages; the runtime excludes unproven opaque state when projecting to a known provider. Text content and client tool requests/results remain portable semantic history.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.SessionAutoModeResolvedData
member.summary: Auto Intent resolution: the concrete model an auto-mode session settled on, and why. Published when Auto settles on a model that differs from the one it last published in the current Auto selection, so a routing check that keeps the same model does not repeat it; selecting a model, switching Auto tiers, or returning to Auto starts a new selection. Lets SDK clients render the chosen model and the full reason it was picked. The core selection fields (chosenModel/reasoningBucket/categoryScores) are stable; the routing-analytics fields (predictedLabel/confidence/candidateModels) mirror the upstream intent service and may evolve, hence the event's experimental stability.

member.summary: Short human-readable sentence from the routing service explaining why this model was chosen, for display alongside the model. Present only when the service supplied one: it is omitted for on-device selections, when the service did not provide an explanation, and when a replayed decision made no routing call. The text is display-only and drawn from a fixed catalogue; several distinct routing categories share identical wording, so it cannot be used to recover the category or keyed on programmatically.
