member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData
member.summary: Effective enterprise managed settings and contributing channels. Session events report applied policy; sessionless resolve reports an account/device snapshot, and compose reports a non-applying preview of candidate documents. Device values take precedence over server values, then the policy helper, per ordinary key, while permissions compose restrictively. Session-local SDK-client policy is included only in session results. Marked experimental while the managed-settings surface stabilizes.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.BypassPermissionsDisabled
member.summary: Whether an explicit enterprise policy restriction disables bypass-permissions ("yolo") mode for this session. Deny-wins across layers; an unresolved policy does not force this on by itself.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.ClientManaged
member.summary: Whether a session-local permissions layer injected by the SDK host was present.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.DeviceManaged
member.summary: Whether an actual device MDM/plist/registry/file managed-settings layer was present.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.FailClosed
member.summary: Whether managed policy could not be determined (e.g. a failed server fetch) and unresolved-policy safeguards remain active. This does not by itself disable bypass-permissions; `bypassPermissionsDisabled` reports only an explicit policy restriction.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.ManagedKeys
member.summary: The setting keys under enterprise management in the effective managed settings (e.g. `model`, `enabledPlugins`, `permissions`). Empty when no managed settings are in force.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.PermissionsAllowIntersected
member.summary: Whether at least two managed sources supplied permission allowlists, so enforcement intersects them and the flattened settings payload omits `permissions.allow`.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.PermissionsContext
member.summary: Reusable retained managed permission policy for managedSettings.permissions.evaluate, including source composition and session-local injection. Provided by live session snapshots; absent in older events. Refresh the context when managed policy changes.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.PolicyHelperCapabilities
member.summary: Explicit Policy Helper structured-failure and recheck capabilities supported by this runtime.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.PolicyHelperFailure
member.summary: The latest unresolved Policy Helper failure for this exact policy context. It remains present across retained-policy refresh failures and clears only after fresh success or authoritative removal.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.PolicyHelperManaged
member.summary: Whether the policy-helper managed-settings layer was present. The policy helper is the weakest channel: it fills keys no enterprise source set and can never replace one.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.SandboxEnabledByUndeterminedPolicy
member.summary: Whether the effective sandbox policy forces the sandbox on *only* because managed policy could not be determined, rather than because the policy requires it. Lets clients tell a user whose `--no-sandbox` was overridden that the sandbox stayed on as a fail-closed fallback, instead of attributing it to an administrator who set no such policy.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.ServerManaged
member.summary: Whether the server (account/org) managed-settings layer was present.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.Settings
member.summary: The effective (resolved) managed settings values, so clients can render exactly what is enforced. Absent when no managed policy is in force.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsResolvedData.Source
member.summary: Channel summary: `server`, `device`, `client`, or `policyHelper` when exactly one channel contributed; `mixed` when multiple channels contributed; otherwise `none`. Consult the per-channel booleans for exact provenance.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsEnforcedData
member.summary: Runtime enforcement of enterprise managed settings: fires when the session blocks or caps a runtime action because enterprise policy governs it, so SDK clients can explain *why* an action was governed. Unlike `session.managed_settings_resolved` (which reports *what* is managed), this reports a concrete governed action — e.g. a user or host tried to turn on bypass permissions or Assisted Permissions while the corresponding policy disables it. Emitted live (not persisted to the session event log) on user/host-initiated attempts only, never for silent policy application. Marked experimental while the managed-settings surface stabilizes.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsEnforcedData.Action
member.summary: The category of runtime action that managed policy governed.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsEnforcedData.Escalation
member.summary: For a `bypass_permissions_blocked` action, which permission-mode or escalation primitive was refused. Absent for actions without a specific primitive.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsEnforcedData.FailClosed
member.summary: Whether the enforcement was forced by fail-closed handling (managed policy could not be determined) rather than an explicit managed setting. When true, `setting` still names the restriction that was applied.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsEnforcedData.Message
member.summary: A human-readable explanation of why the action was governed, suitable for surfacing to the user.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionManagedSettingsEnforcedData.Setting
member.summary: The managed setting key responsible for the enforcement (for example `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` or `permissions.disableAssistedPermissionsMode`).

member.summary: Characters of reply text the latest request streamed, counted as received, so it measures output even when the request was cut off before reporting usage. Tool-call arguments and reasoning are not counted. Absent when no request was dispatched.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.AttemptAge
member.summary: Time since the latest request was dispatched, whether or not it had finished, in milliseconds. Absent when no request was dispatched.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.AttemptCount
member.summary: Number of summarizer model requests dispatched, including retries.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.AttemptSettled
member.summary: Whether the latest request had already returned a response or an error. False when it was still in flight, such as when the compaction deadline cut it off; absent when no request was dispatched.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.Duration
member.summary: Time from the start of the compaction to the decision of its outcome, in milliseconds.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.Idle
member.summary: Time since the latest request's last stream event, or since its dispatch if none arrived, in milliseconds. Absent when no request was dispatched.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.InputShrunk
member.summary: Whether historical attachments and reasoning were dropped from the compaction's input because the session's previous compaction ran out of time.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.InputTokensEstimate
member.summary: Sampled estimate of the input tokens the latest request sent, taken at dispatch, so it is known even when the request was cut off before reporting usage. Absent when no request was dispatched.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.MaxOutputGapAfterAnswer
member.summary: Longest gap between two consecutive outputs of the latest request after its first reply text or tool-call output, in milliseconds. Excludes the still-open gap reported as sinceLastOutputMs; absent without such a gap.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.MaxOutputGapBeforeAnswer
member.summary: Longest gap between two consecutive outputs of the latest request up to its first reply text or tool-call output, including the gap that ends there, in milliseconds. Excludes the still-open gap reported as sinceLastOutputMs; absent without such a gap.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.MaxStreamEventGap
member.summary: Longest gap between two consecutive stream events of the latest request, in milliseconds. Excludes the still-open gap reported as idleMs; absent with fewer than two events.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.OutputEventCount
member.summary: Stream events of the latest request that carried observable output.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.ReasoningChars
member.summary: Characters of reasoning text, summarized or raw, the latest request streamed, counted as received. Encrypted reasoning is not counted. Absent when no request was dispatched.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.SinceLastOutput
member.summary: Time since the latest request's last observable output, in milliseconds. Unlike idleMs, keepalive deltas do not reset it. Absent when no output arrived.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.StreamEventCount
member.summary: Token-bearing stream events the latest request received, keepalive deltas included.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.TimeToFirstAnswerOutput
member.summary: Time from dispatching the latest request to its first reply text or tool-call output, in milliseconds. Reasoning does not count. Absent when no such output arrived.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.TimeToFirstOutput
member.summary: Time from dispatching the latest request to its first observable text, reasoning, or tool-call output, in milliseconds. Absent when no output arrived.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CompactionCompleteSummarizerProgress.TimeToFirstToken
member.summary: Time from dispatching the latest request to its first token-bearing stream event, in milliseconds. Absent when no stream event arrived.

member.summary: Why the run recorded and allowed instead of enforcing.

member.summary: Host operating-system family.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataAccessRecorded.ToolCallId
member.summary: Tool call the access belongs to, for span correlation only. Never exported as a telemetry attribute or metric dimension.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataBypassDecided
member.summary: A request to run outside the process sandbox was resolved. This is what makes an `inactive` `enforcement_state` readable: without it, a command that ran unsandboxed because a person approved a bypass looks identical to one that ran unsandboxed because the session never had a sandbox. Reported only when a sandbox was in force, since bypassing a disabled sandbox bypasses nothing. Carries neither backend nor attestation: the verdict comes from the runtime's own permission flow or the local escalation prompt, not from a containment backend and not from the built-in policy check, so `source` is what records where it came from.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataBypassDecided.Command
member.summary: Command the verdict governs. Populated only when content capture is enabled.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataBypassDecided.Confidence
member.summary: How strong the evidence behind `denialClass` was. Present exactly when `denialClass` is, so a verdict that relaxed the sandbox on a guess is distinguishable from one that relaxed it on a recorded refusal. Named to match `access_denied`, which reports the same pair.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataBypassDecided.Control
member.summary: Always `bypass`.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataBypassDecided.DenialClass
member.summary: Bounded class of the access whose refusal raised this escalation. Omitted for a pre-execution bypass, such as a detached command that cannot be sandboxed and therefore resolves no denial.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataBypassDecided.DeniedResource
member.summary: Resource whose refusal raised this escalation. Populated only when content capture is enabled.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataBypassDecided.EnforcementPoint
member.summary: Runtime subsystem the bypass applies to.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataBypassDecided.Outcome
member.summary: Whether the bypass was granted: `approved` or `declined`. `declined` also covers the cases where nobody answered, since the sandboxed denial stands either way.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataBypassDecided.Platform
member.summary: Host operating-system family.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataBypassDecided.ProcessName
member.summary: Executable image associated with the denial that raised this escalation, normalized to a basename. Populated only when content capture is enabled.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataBypassDecided.Source
member.summary: Where the request originated. Orthogonal to `outcome`.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataBypassDecided.ToolCallId
member.summary: Tool call the decision belongs to, for span correlation only. Never exported as a telemetry attribute or metric dimension.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataPermissiveRetryDecided
member.summary: A permissive retry was resolved. Distinct from `bypass_decided` because this rung never requests a run outside the process sandbox: it relaxes the process container for one run while the sandbox, and with it the network policy, stays attached. Reported for both outcomes, so an escalation the user declined still leaves evidence that the runtime asked and that the sandboxed denial stood.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataPermissiveRetryDecided.Command
member.summary: Command the verdict governs. Populated only when content capture is enabled.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataPermissiveRetryDecided.Confidence
member.summary: How strong the evidence behind `denialClass` was. Present exactly when `denialClass` is.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDecisionDataPermissiveRetryDecided.Control
member.summary: Always `process`: the process container is what this rung relaxes, and the network control is deliberately untouched.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.PermissionSandboxPathGrant
member.summary: A sandbox filesystem policy edit that would let a blocked operation run inside the sandbox instead of outside it. Offered only on a sandbox escalation request whose denial adding this path lifts, and only when managed policy permits the grant. A host accepts it with session.sandbox.grantPathForRequest, which adds the path to the session's sandbox policy and re-runs the operation sandboxed. A host that persists sandbox settings must save the optional policy spelling when present; otherwise it must escape every literal `$` in the concrete path as `$$` before saving that path.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.PermissionSandboxPathGrant.Access
member.summary: Which access the grant confers, and so which policy list the path is added to.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.PermissionSandboxPathGrant.DeniedPath
member.summary: The path the sandbox refused, present only when it differs from path. That happens when a write under a read-only folder moves the folder to the read-write paths, when a path that does not exist yet is granted through its nearest existing folder, because the OS sandbox cannot grant a path before it exists, and when either is spelled through a symlink, because a grant covers its path as written, so path is then the resolved location. Hosts should then name path in the offer, since the denial names this one.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.PermissionSandboxPathGrant.Path
member.summary: Absolute path to add to the sandbox filesystem policy.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.PermissionSandboxPathGrant.PersistedPath
member.summary: Policy spelling to persist for the grant. This can differ from path when a managed allowlist names the same location through an environment expression. Hosts that persist sandbox settings must save this value when present. When it is absent, they must escape every literal `$` in path as `$$` before saving path so the policy grammar does not interpret it as an environment reference.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.PermissionSandboxPathGrant.RemovedReadonlyPaths
member.summary: readonlyPaths entries the grant removes, exactly as written in the policy, because a read-only entry for the same location would otherwise keep the path read-only. A host that persists the path must remove these entries from its stored readonlyPaths too.

member.summary: URLs that may be accessed by the command.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.PermissionRequestShell.RequestSandboxBypass
member.summary: True when the tool is asking to run this command outside the sandbox, either because the command detaches and cannot be sandboxed at all, or because a sandboxed run looked blocked (host opted in via sandbox.allowBypass). The model cannot ask for this; only the tool raises it. This is a request, not a grant: the command runs unsandboxed only if the user approves this permission request. Hosts should highlight the elevated risk in the approval UI.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.PermissionRequestShell.RequestSandboxBypassReason
member.summary: What the tool tells the user about the bypass on offer: which policy rule blocked the call, or why it cannot be sandboxed. Only meaningful when requestSandboxBypass is true.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.PermissionRequestShell.RequestSandboxPermissive
member.summary: True when the requested escalation is a permissive retry rather than a full bypass: the command re-runs inside the sandbox with its file and process restrictions recording instead of blocking, while the network policy stays enforced. Always accompanied by requestSandboxBypass, so hosts that do not recognize this field still treat the request as the escalation it is. Hosts that do recognize it must not describe the command as running outside the sandbox, which would overstate the privilege being granted.

member.summary: Human-readable description of why the URL is being accessed.

member.summary: Whether managed policy requires a human response and forbids host auto-approval.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.PermissionPromptRequestUrl.ParentDomainPattern
member.summary: Wildcard pattern covering the registrable domain of the URL and its subdomains, for example https://*.example.com for https://api.example.com/x. The runtime computes it from the Public Suffix List, keeping the URL's scheme and non-default port, so every host offers the same scope. Absent when no parent-domain approval can be offered safely (IP addresses, private-network names, public suffixes) and for sandbox-bypass requests. Hosts may offer it as a broader alternative to approving the exact origin for the running session and, when the user chooses it, return it as the domain of an approve-for-session response. It is session-only: the runtime matches it by registrable domain, so a subdomain the Public Suffix List lists as a separate owner (for example a bucket under s3.amazonaws.com) is not covered, and the runtime never persists it. Do not offer it as a permanent approval; an approve-permanently response carrying this exact pattern is kept for the session only and writes nothing to settings. The pattern also matches the registrable domain itself.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.PermissionPromptRequestUrl.RedirectedFrom
member.summary: Immediately preceding URL when this prompt is for a redirect target.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.PermissionPromptRequestUrl.RequestSandboxBypass
member.summary: True when the tool is asking to run this URL fetch outside the sandbox, after the network policy denied the approved URL or the sandbox proxy could not reach it (host opted in via sandbox.allowBypass). The model cannot ask for this; only the tool raises it. This is a request, not a grant: the fetch runs only if the user approves this permission request. Hosts should highlight the elevated risk in the approval UI.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.PermissionPromptRequestUrl.RequestSandboxBypassReason
member.summary: What the tool tells the user about the bypass on offer: which policy rule blocked the call, or why it cannot be sandboxed. Only meaningful when requestSandboxBypass is true.

member.summary: Gets the value associated with this .

member.summary: The sandbox's own denial capture recorded the refused access. The strongest evidence available: the kernel observed it, not the runtime.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SandboxDenialConfidence.PolicyCorroborated
member.summary: The command named a path that the effective policy independently denies. No capture confirmed it, but the policy did.

member.summary: The failure carried a fingerprint the sandbox itself emits, so the sandbox is known to have refused something even though the resource was not confirmed.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.JsonRpc
member.summary: A lightweight JSON-RPC 2.0 implementation covering only the features used by this SDK to talk to the Copilot CLI. Messages are framed using the LSP-style header convention (Content-Length: N\r\n\r\n followed by N bytes of JSON body) — the same wire format used by the Language Server Protocol and the Copilot CLI's other language SDKs (Go, Node, Python). This is not a general-purpose JSON-RPC stack: it is narrowly scoped to the methods, transports, and framing the CLI uses.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.NetworkConfig
member.summary: Network callbacks through which the SDK host takes over parts of the runtime's networking, for example when the runtime runs in WSL or a container and should use VS Code's proxy settings and the host's Kerberos tickets.

remarks.para: Each configured callback replaces the runtime's own handling for the traffic in ; without it, the runtime handles that part itself. The SDK registers the configured callbacks during , before sessions can be created, and only when at least one is configured.

Exceptions thrown by a callback, including cancellation not requested through the supplied , fail the request. Callbacks are started on a thread-pool thread and may block, for example while prompting for credentials. The supplied is cancelled when the runtime stops waiting (it cancels the request, for example when its wait times out) or the connection closes, and a callback not yet started by then is not started. The SDK then stops awaiting the callback and ignores any later result.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.NetworkConfig.Scope
member.remarks: Only one connection at a time can hold , so startup fails if another client holds it. The scope applies to the whole registration, which ends when the connection closes.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.NetworkConfig.ResolveProxy
member.summary: Gets the callback that returns the proxies for as a PAC-style list such as PROXY proxy.example:8080; HTTPS proxy.example:443; DIRECT (the format of Electron's session.resolveProxy); return DIRECT for a direct connection, or to let the runtime resolve the proxy itself, as if no callback were registered.
member.remarks: is the request target as a PAC script sees it: without credentials or fragment, and for https and wss also without path and query. Entry types the runtime doesn't support, such as SOCKS and QUIC, are skipped. The callback decides every request that would otherwise follow ambient proxy settings: proxy environment variables, NO_PROXY and operating-system proxy settings are not consulted unless it returns , and a failing callback fails the request rather than connecting directly. Requests to loopback targets, and requests with an explicitly configured proxy, never consult it. The runtime caches answers, including , for 5 seconds and waits at most 10 seconds for the callback.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.NetworkConfig.AuthenticateNegotiate
member.summary: Gets the callback that returns a fresh, single-use base64 SPNEGO token without the Negotiate prefix for a proxy's Negotiate challenge, or when credentials are unavailable.
member.remarks: The runtime then does not look up Kerberos credentials itself, so a missing token or a failing callback fails the request. uses the platform-independent service/host[@REALM] form; validate it before issuing credentials. Tokens must not be logged or persisted. The runtime waits at most 30 seconds for the callback (less when the request's own deadline is sooner). The callback supplies the initial SPNEGO token only; exchanges requiring continuation tokens are not supported. Proxies chosen by are authenticated the same way.

member.summary: Registers a callback for session events.
member.param: A callback to be invoked when a session event occurs.
member.returns: An that, when disposed, unsubscribes the handler.
member.exception: Thrown if the session has been disposed.
Thrown if session event delivery has stopped.

remarks.para: Events include assistant messages, tool executions, errors, and session state changes. Multiple handlers can be registered and will all receive events.
Handlers are invoked serially in event-arrival order on a background thread. A handler will never be called concurrently with itself or with other handlers on the same session.
Unsubscribing or closing the session releases handlers that have not been admitted for dispatch. A handler already admitted may finish; disposal does not wait for it.

member.summary: Registers custom tool handlers for this session.
member.param: A collection of AI function declarations available to the assistant.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.CopilotSession.SetToolsAsync(System.Collections.Generic.ICollection{Microsoft.Extensions.AI.AIFunctionDeclaration},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Replaces the complete custom tool list supplied by this SDK client for the live session.
member.param: The same tool declarations accepted by when creating or resuming a session. Passing an empty collection removes all externally implemented tools supplied by this client.

A token that cancels the call. Cancelling while an earlier replacement is still in flight sends nothing. Once the request is sent, cancelling only stops the wait: an accepted replacement still installs its handlers.
member.returns: A task that completes after the runtime accepts the replacement.

remarks.para: This is a complete replacement for this client's externally implemented tools only. Built-in tools, MCP/plugin tools, extension-discovered tools, subagent tools, and tools supplied by other connections are unchanged. The wire definitions are the same as the tools supplied when creating or resuming a session.

Tool handlers switch when the runtime's acceptance response arrives, before subsequent tool requests are dispatched. Tool calls already running finish with the handlers that started them. If the runtime rejects the replacement, the previous handlers remain installed and the exception is propagated. Concurrent calls are applied in order. Acceptance after local retirement fails the replacement without restoring its handlers.

The agent sees the new tools from its next model request, which can fall within a turn in progress. A model request already in flight was made with the previous tools, so the agent can still call a tool you removed. This session doesn't answer that call, and it can stay pending until the turn is aborted. If a running turn might still call a tool you remove, replace tools while the session is idle.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.CopilotSession.SetAutoTierAsync(System.Nullable{GitHub.Copilot.AutoTier},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Changes the Auto routing preference without changing the selected model.

remarks.para: The runtime does not apply the preference immediately. It records the request and commits it only when a later user turn using the auto model successfully obtains a usable model from the provider. A pending status therefore confirms that the request was accepted, not that it took effect.

Watch for the outcome through the session.model_change event on success, or the ephemeral session.auto_tier_switch_failed event on failure. You can also read the current committed and in-flight state at any time with session.Rpc.Model.GetCurrentAsync.
Only the most recent request survives: issuing a new request replaces any earlier one that has not yet been claimed by a turn.

member.param: Routing preference to activate, or to return to the provider's default Auto routing.
Optional cancellation token.
member.returns: The runtime's immediate acknowledgement and Auto preference snapshot.

example.code: var result = await session.SetAutoTierAsync(AutoTier.Intelligence);

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.CopilotSession.DisposeAsync
member.summary: Closes this session and releases all in-memory resources (event handlers, tool handlers, permission handlers).
member.returns: A task representing the dispose operation.

remarks.para: The caller should ensure the session is idle (e.g., has returned) before disposing. If the session is not idle, in-flight event handlers or tool handlers may observe failures.

Session state on disk (conversation history, planning state, artifacts) is preserved, so the conversation can be resumed later by calling with the session ID. To permanently remove all session data including files on disk, use instead.
After calling this method, the session object can no longer be used.

Stops subscribed event delivery and releases queued events and subscriptions. Handlers already admitted for dispatch may finish; disposal does not wait for them. Pending response waiters fail if the session closes before their final response.

member.summary: Sends a message with a JSON Schema inferred from and deserializes the final response into that type.

Options used both for schema inference and deserialization. Defaults to , as for custom tools. For Native AOT, supply options with a source-generated type resolver.

Property naming, converters, required members and nullable annotations follow the supplied serialization contracts. Deserialization is not full JSON Schema validation; apply application-specific validation to the returned value where needed. The supplied message options are not modified.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.InProcessRuntimeConnection.RunOnUiThread
member.summary: Schedules the supplied native action exactly once on the UI thread (the process main thread on macOS), completing only after it returns. The action can block while native UI is open. No authentication data crosses this callback. Other in-process clients may share this process-wide capability. Required for OneAuth interactive authentication on macOS. This general-purpose scheduler may also be used for other runtime-owned native UI operations. Temporary OneAuth workaround; this API may be removed if no longer needed.

member.name: F:GitHub.Copilot.CopilotClientMode.Empty
member.summary:
Disables optional features by default. The app must explicitly opt into anything it needs. Required for any scenario where CLI-like ambient behavior is unsafe (e.g., multi-user servers).
When this mode is selected:
The client constructor requires or to be set.
must be supplied on every session — no tools are exposed by default.
The SDK injects safe defaults for ambient session features (telemetry, custom instructions, plugins, environment context, etc.).
COPILOT_DISABLE_KEYTAR=1 is set on the spawned runtime so credentials are persisted to COPILOT_HOME rather than a process-wide system keychain.

member.name: F:GitHub.Copilot.CopilotClientMode.CopilotCli
member.summary:
Uses defaults equivalent to GitHub Copilot CLI. The default. Useful when building a coding agent that shares sessions with Copilot CLI.
Do not use this mode for server-based multi-user applications — the default coding agent has tools and capabilities that operate across sessions and can access the host OS environment.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CopilotClientOptions.UseLoggedInUser
member.summary: Whether to use the logged-in user for authentication. When true, the runtime will attempt to use stored OAuth tokens or gh CLI auth. When false, only explicit tokens such as GitHubToken are used; environment variable tokens (COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN) are ignored. Default: true (but defaults to false when GitHubToken is provided).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CopilotClientOptions.OnListModels

member.summary: Custom session filesystem provider configuration. When set, the client registers as the session filesystem provider on connect, routing session-scoped file I/O through per-session handlers created via .

member.summary: Configures interception of the LLM inference requests the runtime would otherwise issue itself (for both CAPI and BYOK providers). When set, the client registers a client-global LLM inference handler on connect, so every model-layer HTTP / WebSocket request is routed to this subclass instead of the runtime's own outbound call.

member.summary: Server-wide idle timeout for sessions in seconds. Sessions without activity for this duration are automatically cleaned up. Set to 0 or leave as to disable (sessions live indefinitely). This option is only used when the SDK spawns the runtime; it is ignored when connecting to an external runtime via .

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CopilotClientOptions.ClientInfo
member.summary: Declares the integrating application's identity, forwarded to the runtime on the server.connect handshake. Declaring it lets the telemetry the runtime emits on this connection be attributed to a consistent surface (the application and its Copilot integration) instead of the runtime's own build. All fields are optional; leave it to keep the runtime's default attribution.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.CopilotClientOptions.Clone
member.summary: Creates a shallow clone of this instance.
member.remarks: Mutable collection properties are copied into new collection instances so that modifications to those collections on the clone do not affect the original. Other reference-type properties (for example delegates and the logger) are not deep-cloned; the original and the clone will share those objects.

item.description: Return null from the hook handler: preserve existing _meta (no-op).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.ProviderConfig.HasBearerTokenProvider
member.summary: Wire-only flag, emitted automatically when is set, that tells the runtime to request a token over the session-scoped providerToken.getToken RPC before each outbound request to this provider. Derived from ; internal and never part of the public API.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.ProviderConfig.BearerTokenProvider
member.summary: Per-request callback that resolves a bearer token on demand for this BYOK provider (for example via Azure Managed Identity). The Copilot SDK takes no identity dependency: supply a callback backed by your own identity library. Never serialized — setting it makes the SDK send hasBearerTokenProvider: true on the wire and answer the runtime's providerToken.getToken requests. When set alongside , , or , this callback takes precedence: the runtime applies the token it returns as the Authorization: Bearer header for each request without sending the static credential or running the command.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CapiSessionOptions.EnableWebSocketResponses
member.summary: When , forces the HTTP Responses transport for the CAPI Responses API instead of the default WebSocket transport.
member.remarks: WebSocket transport is the default for CAPI Responses API requests when the model advertises the ws:/responses endpoint. Set this to for users behind proxies where WebSockets fail. Setting it to is equivalent to setting the COPILOT_CLI_DISABLE_WEBSOCKET_RESPONSES environment variable. The option is scoped under the capi namespace because a single session can host multiple providers, such as CAPI and BYOK, so transport choice is provider-level.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.CapiSessionOptions.AutoTier
member.summary: Routing tier for model auto with V2 Auto.
member.remarks: Requires a runtime that supports Auto tiers; it has no effect outside V2 Auto. When omitted, the runtime uses its default on create and restores the last committed tier on cold resume. On resident resume, a different tier requests a safe switch that takes effect after resume succeeds and never disturbs a turn that is already running. To change the preference on a live session, use .

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.NamedProviderConfig

A named BYOK provider connection (transport + credentials only), referenced by entries via .
Unlike the singular, whole-session — which bypasses Copilot API authentication — named providers are additive and coexist with Copilot API auth, so models from CAPI and one or more BYOK providers can be mixed within a single session and across sub-agents. Combining named providers/models with is rejected.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.ManagedSettingsPermissions.LimitTo
member.summary: Closed-world host boundary expressed as Domain(hostname), Domain(IP), or Domain(*.example.com) rules. Schemes, ports, paths, queries, and fragments are rejected. Multiple managed layers intersect their lists. A present empty list denies all hosts.

member.name: T:GitHub.Copilot.ManagedSettings
member.summary: Managed-settings layer injected at session startup. Currently carries only a object.
member.remarks: This layer is startup-only and is not persisted with the session. It must be re-supplied on to remain in effect; omitting it on resume clears the previously injected layer. It can be combined with . Older runtimes may ignore this additive field, so hosts must not rely on injected policy until they ship a compatible runtime.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.AutoModeRecovery
member.summary: Opt in to runtime-owned recovery of an eligible active request using Auto. Requires and a positive session.Capabilities.Ui.AutoModeRecovery acknowledgment. Unsupported enrollment rejects create/resume and detaches the session. Defaults to false; re-supply when resuming. Consent has no runtime deadline. Do not resend or rewind.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.EnableMcpApps
member.summary:
Enable MCP Apps (SEP-1865) UI passthrough on this session.
When true and the runtime has MCP Apps enabled (via the MCP_APPS feature flag or COPILOT_MCP_APPS=true environment override), the runtime adds the mcp-apps capability to the session, which causes it to advertise the extensions.io.modelcontextprotocol/ui extension to MCP servers (so they expose _meta.ui.resourceUri on tools) and to expose the session.rpc.mcp.apps.{listTools,callTool,readResource,setHostContext,getHostContext,diagnose} JSON-RPC methods.
If the runtime gate is off, the opt-in is silently dropped server-side (the runtime logs a warning); the session is created normally but the MCP Apps surface is unavailable. Inspect the runtime's capabilities.ui.mcpApps on the create/resume response to detect this.
SDK consumers MUST set this to true only when they have an iframe renderer that can display ui:// MCP App bundles. Setting it without a renderer will cause MCP servers to register UI-enabled tool variants the consumer cannot display.

When false, only non-streaming sub-agent events and subagent.* lifecycle events are forwarded; streaming deltas from sub-agents are suppressed. Default: true.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.ImageGeneration
member.summary: Non-persisted image generation opt-in. Re-supply after runtime restart.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.Memory
member.summary: Configuration for session memory. When set, controls whether the session can read and write persistent memory.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.OnEvent
member.summary: Optional event handler registered on the session before the session.create / session.resume RPC is issued, ensuring early events are delivered.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.CreateSessionFsProvider
member.summary: Supplies a handler for session filesystem operations. This is used only when is configured.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.GitHubToken
member.summary: GitHub token for per-session authentication. When provided, the runtime resolves this token into a full GitHub identity and stores it on the session for content exclusion, model routing, and quota checks.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.GitHubTokenProvider
member.summary: Gets or sets a callback that acquires session-scoped GitHub tokens on demand. Initial cancellation, callback errors, and invalid token responses reject session creation or resume instead of falling back to ambient authentication. This cannot be combined with .

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.ExpAssignments
member.summary: ExP assignment ("flight") data injected by a trusted integrator, in the same JSON shape the Copilot CLI fetches from the experimentation service (CopilotExpAssignmentResponse). When provided, the runtime feeds it into the same feature-flag path as CLI-fetched assignments and stamps it onto telemetry and the CAPI request header. When unset, the session does not block on ExP. Intended for out-of-process integrators that fetch ExP data themselves; malformed payloads are dropped by the runtime (fail-open). Serialized on the wire as expAssignments.
member.remarks: This is an internal/trusted-integrator option and is hidden from editor completion. It is not part of the broadly advertised public surface.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.FeatureFlags
member.summary: Feature-flag values resolved by the host for this session. Re-supply them when resuming after a runtime restart.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.EnableManagedSettings
member.summary: Opt-in: when true, the runtime self-fetches enterprise managed settings (bypass-permissions policy) at session bootstrap using the session's . Requires to be set; if omitted, the runtime is expected to reject session creation (fail-closed). When unset, behaves exactly as before. Serialized on the wire as enableManagedSettings.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.ExcludedManagedSettings
member.summary: Exact dotted setting paths excluded from fetched, device, and policy-helper policy. Host-injected policy and availability checks are unaffected. Not persisted; re-supply on resume, where omission restores full enforcement. Use EnableManagedSettings to enable self-fetching.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.EnforceManagedModelDefaults
member.summary: When true, enforces locked managed model controls for this session. Conflicting model changes are rejected; overridable managed defaults remain mutable.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.InteractiveUser
member.summary: Declares that a human drives this session's conversation, enabling user-message analysis telemetry for user-authored messages. Automated messages remain excluded. Defaults to false for SDK sessions; ignored for cloud sessions and when resuming a session already active in the runtime process.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.PermissionMode
member.summary: Permission mode applied before the session's first turn: before session creation returns, and before a resume continues pending work. Uses the same checks as session.Rpc.Permissions.SetModeAsync; a mode that managed policy or session capabilities refuse leaves the current mode in place. reports whether it was applied and the authoritative mode. Leave unset to keep the default mode on create, or the restored mode on resume. Not supported for cloud sessions.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.ManagedSettings
member.summary: Optional managed-settings layer injected at session bootstrap. Currently carries a permissions object that composes restrictively with any server- or device-level managed settings. This layer is startup-only and is not persisted: it must be re-supplied on resume to remain in effect, and omitting it on resume clears the previously injected layer. Can be combined with . Serialized on the wire as managedSettings.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.Canvases
member.summary: Canvas declarations advertised by this connection. The runtime forwards these to the agent and routes inbound canvas.* requests for any declared canvas to .

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.RequestCanvasRenderer
member.summary: When , asks the host to expose canvas renderer tools for this session. The host typically grants this only to trusted clients.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.RequestExtensions
member.summary: When , asks the host to expose extension-discovery tools for this session. The host typically grants this only to trusted clients.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.ExtensionSdkPath
member.summary: Optional override path to a copilot-sdk/ folder to inject into extension subprocesses for this session in place of the bundled SDK. When unset or invalid (missing folder, or missing index.js / extension.js), the runtime falls back to the bundled SDK without throwing. Takes precedence over any server-level default.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.ExtensionInfo
member.summary: Stable extension identity for canvas/tool providers on this connection. Required when is set so the runtime can attribute declared canvases back to this provider.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.CanvasProvider
member.summary: Stable identity for a host/SDK connection that supplies built-in canvases. When set, the runtime uses verbatim as the agent-facing canvas extension id, so canvases declared on a control connection survive reconnect and CLI restart. Honored on session create and resume.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.CanvasHandler
member.summary: Provider-side canvas lifecycle handler. The SDK routes inbound canvas.open / canvas.close / canvas.action.invoke requests to this handler.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfigBase.OnMcpAuthRequest
member.summary: Optional handler for MCP OAuth requests from MCP servers. When provided, the SDK can satisfy MCP server OAuth requests with host-provided token data or cancellation.

member.summary: Optional session identifier; a new ID is generated if not provided.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfig.Name
member.summary: Names the session at creation, as session.name.set would, and is validated the same way: non-empty, no leading or trailing whitespace, at most 100 UTF-16 units, no control characters, and no double quotes. A name also makes the session persist from the start, so it can be listed and resumed without ever running a turn. Local sessions only: cloud creation rejects it.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfig.Cloud
member.summary: Creates a remote session in the cloud instead of a local session. The optional repository is associated with the cloud session.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfig.TrustWorkingDirectory
member.summary: Trusts the working directory for this session ("session") or persistently for the user ("user"). Omitted leaves existing folder trust unchanged.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfig.RefreshCustomInstructions
member.summary: When true, invalidates process-wide custom-instruction discovery caches before constructing this new session. Omitted or false reuses the caches. Other sessions in this runtime may observe updated instructions on later turns or discovery. This does not watch files or override instruction enablement.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.SessionConfig.Clone
member.summary: Creates a shallow clone of this instance.
member.remarks: Mutable collection properties are copied into new collection instances so that modifications to those collections on the clone do not affect the original. Other reference-type properties (for example provider configuration, system messages, hooks, infinite session configuration, and delegates) are not deep-cloned; the original and the clone will share those nested objects, and changes to them may affect both.

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.

member.summary: Initializes a new instance of by copying the properties of the specified instance.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.ResumeSessionConfig.SuppressResumeEvent
member.summary: When true, the session.resume event is not emitted. Default: false (resume event is emitted).

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.ResumeSessionConfig.ContinuePendingWork
member.summary:
When , instructs the runtime to continue any tool calls or permission prompts that were still pending when the session was last suspended. When (the default), the runtime treats pending work as interrupted on resume. Completed tool results already durably recorded by the runtime are preserved.
When , pending permission requests and external tool calls wait for caller-supplied results via the corresponding low-level RPC methods. Resuming does not re-emit restored permission requests or re-invoke permission handlers or already-dispatched external tool callbacks. If a pending call was recorded as SDK-handler-backed and resume registers a handler for that tool, the abandoned callback is interrupted, never replayed. Handlerless calls remain pending. To supply an abandoned callback's result manually, resume without a handler for it. Older requests without recorded callback ownership also remain pending.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.ResumeSessionConfig.AllowTranscriptRecovery
P:GitHub.Copilot.ResumeSessionConfig.OpenCanvases
member.summary: Snapshot of canvases that were already open when the session was suspended. When provided on resume, the runtime can rehydrate canvas state so consumers do not need to re-open canvases that were active before the previous shutdown.

member.summary: The prompt text to send to the assistant.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.MessageOptions.Attachments
member.summary: File or data attachments to include with the message.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.MessageOptions.Mode
member.summary: How to deliver the message. "enqueue" (default) appends to the message queue; "immediate" interjects during an in-progress turn.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.MessageOptions.AgentMode
member.summary: The UI mode the agent was in when this message was sent (for example "plan", "autopilot"). Defaults to the session's current mode when unset.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.MessageOptions.Source
member.summary: The message's origin. When unset, the field is omitted and the runtime defaults to user input. This tags message provenance; it does not replace the session's system prompt or change delivery mode.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.MessageOptions.RequestHeaders
member.summary: Custom per-turn HTTP headers for outbound model requests.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.MessageOptions.DisplayPrompt
member.summary: If provided, this is shown in the timeline instead of .

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.MessageOptions.ClientTurnId
member.summary: Opaque caller-chosen ID for the turn this message starts. The runtime copies it unchanged into _meta["com.github.copilot/turnId"] on every MCP tools/call made while serving that turn, including calls from sub-agents and Autopilot continuations. When a running turn consumes the message as visible user steering, the value (or its absence) replaces the turn's ID from the next model call onward. The user.message event for the message echoes it as clientTurnId and is persisted like other events; the value stamped on MCP calls is held in memory only and is not restored on resume.

member.name: P:GitHub.Copilot.MessageOptions.ResponseSchema
member.summary: Optional provider-native JSON Schema for this turn, including tool continuations. The schema is passed unchanged with the name "response" and strict enforcement requested. Ordinary immediate steering retains the active run's schema and origin even when promoted to a follow-up after the model request finishes. An immediate message must not specify its own schema, even while idle. Independent sends and context resets do not inherit this schema; it is not a persisted session default. Use for advanced response-format options.

member.name: M:GitHub.Copilot.MessageOptions.Clone
member.summary: Creates a shallow clone of this instance.
member.remarks: Mutable collection properties are copied into new collection instances so that modifications to those collections on the clone do not affect the original. Other reference-type properties (for example attachment items) are not deep-cloned; the original and the clone will share those nested objects.
